user
Ты ревьюишь волны 4 («Сохранность») и 5 («Папка, меню, настройки») проекта Plain — личного Markdown reader/editor для Windows (Tauri 2 + React 19 + TS + Vite + CodeMirror 6 + Rust). Ничего не правь — только читай и пиши отзыв.

Контекст: личный проект для одного человека; норма — `ТЗ-Plain.md` v2.2. **§8 — единственный раздел, где не экономим на корректности: приложение не теряет и не портит текст.** Остальное — §1.3, §4, §6, §7, §10, §12, §13, §14. Код волны 4: `src-tauri/src/{fs.rs,watch.rs,lib.rs}`, `src/app/{save.ts,drafts.ts,session.ts,watcher.ts,close.ts,fs.ts,eol.ts}`, `src/ui/{Modal.tsx,Recovery.tsx,dialogs.css}`, `src/editor/index.ts`. Волны 5: `src-tauri/src/{tree.rs,search.rs}`, `src/library/**`, `src/app/{registry.ts,menu.ts,zoom.ts,settings.ts}`, `src/ui/{FileTree,QuickSearch,FolderSearch,Settings}.tsx`, `src/editor/{toolbar.ts,remote.ts}`, `src-tauri/capabilities/default.json`. Приложение запущено живьём и работает: сохранение проверено байт-в-байт, конфликт, восстановление черновика после kill, cp1251→utf-8. Тесты зелёные (174 vitest, 28 cargo).

Что ищем, по приоритету:
1. **Потеря/порча текста** (§8): гонки между idle-flush текста из редактора и снимком для записи (`save.ts` `write`/`settle`, `flushActiveEditor`), последовательность записей, `baseHash` после успешной/неуспешной записи, конфликт vs `missing` vs `allow_missing`, `ReplaceFileW` + temp-файл (`fs.rs` `replace_with`: что при падении между `keep()` и `ReplaceFileW`, что с правами/атрибутами, что если target — symlink/read-only), кодировки (UTF-16 ручной энкодер, cp1251 с непредставимыми символами — `encode_rs` подставит `&#…;`! — это порча текста без предупреждения?), `apply_eol` (`\r` внутри строки), финальный перевод строки, BOM. Черновики: когда удаляются, что при крэше во время записи черновика, `don't save`, восстановление и порядок с восстановлением сессии. Watcher: свои события vs внешние по хэшу, тихая перезагрузка с правками в read-режиме, `deleted on disk`.
2. Логические дыры в закрытии (`close.ts`, `onCloseRequested`), сессии (`session.ts`: что пишется при закрытии, LRU), настройках (`settings.ts` запись debounce 300 мс при закрытии окна).
3. Capabilities/scope (`default.json`): `opener:allow-open-path` `**`, `fs:scope`, `core:menu`, `allow_asset_dir` расширяет fs-scope на папку — приемлемо для личного, но отметь лишнее.
4. Волна 5: `search.rs` (regex DoS не важен — файлы свои; но лимиты/усечение/`from_utf8_lossy`), `tree.rs` (симлинки, ошибки доступа), `registry.ts` как единый источник команд (дубли хоткеев между реестром, CodeMirror keymap и меню — агент перенёс `Ctrl+F/H/G` в реестр через `remote.ts`; проверь, что ничего не вызывается дважды и ничего не потерялось), `menu.ts` (пересборка меню на каждое изменение `recent` — утечки?), `toolbar.ts` (утечки DOM, позиционирование).
5. Оверинжиниринг — критерий «окупится ли за месяц использования одним человеком».

Формат: список находок, каждая — файл:строка, суть, почему важно, предложение. Раздели на «критично / стоит поправить / вкусовщина». Не пересказывай код, не хвали. По-русски, термины по-английски.

FILE src/app/save.ts
1: // Ctrl+S and everything around it (spec 8). The rules, in order:
2: // a clean document is never written; the snapshot that goes to disk is taken
3: // before the write and compared to the buffer after it; the base hash always
4: // follows a successful write; nothing the user did not touch changes.
5: 
6: import { save as saveDialog } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog";
7: import { flushActiveEditor, isDirty, markSaved, renameBuffer, replaceText } from "../editor";
8: import { dropBuffer } from "../editor/buffers";
9: import { dropDraft, writeDraft } from "./drafts";
10: import { inTauri } from "./env";
11: import { encodingLabel, isLegacy, normalizeEol, serialize } from "./eol";
12: import { docFields, fsError, readFile, writeFileAtomic } from "./fs";
13: import { dirname, pathKey } from "./paths";
14: import { activeDoc, useStore, type Doc } from "./store";
15: 
16: /* -------------------------------------------------------------- plumbing */
17: 
18: /**
19:  * Writes of one document never overlap: a second Ctrl+S waits for the first
20:  * (spec 8). Rust serializes writes too; this keeps the store consistent.
21:  */
22: const queues = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>();
23: 
24: function queued<T>(id: string, run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
25:   const previous = queues.get(id) ?? Promise.resolve();
26:   const next = previous.then(run, run);
27:   queues.set(id, next);
28:   void next.catch(() => undefined).then(() => {
29:     if (queues.get(id) === next) queues.delete(id);
30:   });
31:   return next;
32: }
33: 
34: function doc(id: string): Doc | undefined {
35:   return useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
36: }
37: 
38: /* ------------------------------------------------------------- the write */
39: 
40: /**
41:  * The base hash always follows a successful write, or the next save would
42:  * conflict with our own file (spec 8). Then the buffer is compared to the
43:  * snapshot: unchanged means saved and the draft can go, changed means the
44:  * document is still unsaved and the draft stays with the new base hash.
45:  */
46: function settle(id: string, snapshot: string, hash: string): void {
47:   const store = useStore.getState();
48:   markSaved(id, snapshot);
49:   // Anything typed while the write was in flight counts against the snapshot,
50:   // so the editor is read now rather than on its next idle callback.
51:   flushActiveEditor();
52:   const current = doc(id);
53:   if (!current) return;
54:   const dirty = normalizeEol(current.text) !== snapshot;
55:   store.updateDoc(id, { savedText: snapshot, baseHash: hash, dirty, deleted: false });
56:   store.dismissBanner("conflict");
57:   store.dismissBanner("save-failed");
58:   if (dirty) void writeDraft(id);
59:   else void dropDraft(current);
60: }
61: 
62: interface Target {
63:   path: string;
64:   baseHash: string | null;
65:   allowMissing?: boolean;
66: }
67: 
68: async function write(id: string, target: Target): Promise<boolean> {
69:   const current = doc(id);
70:   if (!current) return false;
71:   const snapshot = normalizeEol(current.text);
72: 
73:   try {
74:     const hash = await writeFileAtomic({
75:       path: target.path,
76:       text: serialize(snapshot, current.eol),
77:       encoding: current.encoding,
78:       bom: current.bom,
79:       eol: current.eol,
80:       baseHash: target.baseHash,
81:       allowMissing: target.allowMissing ?? false,
82:     });
83:     settle(id, snapshot, hash);
84:     // One of the two allowed transformations, and it says so (spec 1.3).
85:     if (current.mixedEol) {
86:       useStore.getState().updateDoc(id, { mixedEol: false });
87:       useStore.getState().setMessage(`line endings normalized to ${current.eol}`);
88:     }
89:     return true;
90:   } catch (error) {
91:     const failure = fsError(error);
92:     if (failure.kind === "conflict") {
93:       showConflict(id);
94:       return false;
95:     }
96:     // Deleted from under us, and the buffer holds edits: put the file back.
97:     if (failure.kind === "missing") {
98:       const back = await write(id, { ...target, allowMissing: true });
99:       if (back) useStore.getState().setNote("recreated");
100:       return back;
101:     }
102:     useStore.getState().showBanner({
103:       id: "save-failed",
104:       text: `couldn't save - ${failure.message}`,
105:       actions: [
106:         { label: "retry", run: () => void save(id) },
107:         { label: "save as:", run: () => void saveAs(id) },
108:       ],
109:     });
110:     return false;
111:   }
112: }
113: 
114: /* ------------------------------------------------------------- commands */
115: 
116: export function saveActive(): Promise<boolean> {
117:   flushActiveEditor();
118:   const current = activeDoc(useStore.getState());
119:   return current ? save(current.id) : Promise.resolve(true);
120: }
121: 
122: /** `Ctrl+S`. Resolves to false when the document is still unsaved. */
123: export function save(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
124:   flushActiveEditor();
125:   return queued(id, async () => {
126:     const current = doc(id);
127:     if (!current) return true;
128:     // A buffer that was never on disk goes through the Save As dialog (6).
129:     if (!current.path) return saveAs(id);
130:     if (current.readOnly) {
131:       useStore.getState().setMessage("read-only - use save as:");
132:       return false;
133:     }
134:     // 8: a clean document is not written at all, and says nothing.
135:     if (!isDirty(id, current.text)) return true;
136:     if (isLegacy(current.encoding)) {
137:       askAboutEncoding(current);
138:       return false;
139:     }
140:     // Deleted from under us: the buffer's edits go back to disk (spec 6).
141:     const recreate = current.deleted;
142:     const written = await write(id, {
143:       path: current.path,
144:       baseHash: current.baseHash,
145:       allowMissing: recreate,
146:     });
147:     if (written && recreate) useStore.getState().setNote("recreated");
148:     return written;
149:   });
150: }
151: 
152: /** `Ctrl+Shift+S`, and the way out of every conflict. */
153: export async function saveAs(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
154:   if (!inTauri) return false;
155:   flushActiveEditor();
156:   const store = useStore.getState();
157:   const current = doc(id);
158:   if (!current) return false;
159: 
160:   const folder = current.path ? dirname(current.path) : store.libraryPath;
161:   const suggestion = current.path ?? (folder ? `${folder}\\${current.title}.md` : `${current.title}.md`);
162:   const extensions = store.settings.library.extensions.map((e) => e.replace(/^\./, ""));
163:   const picked = await saveDialog({
164:     defaultPath: suggestion,
165:     filters: [{ name: "markdown", extensions }],
166:   });
167:   if (typeof picked !== "string") return false;
168: 
169:   const nextId = pathKey(picked);
170:   const previous = { id: current.id, path: current.path };
171: 
172:   if (nextId !== current.id) {
173:     // Saving over a file that is already open would give it two buffers.
174:     const clash = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === nextId);
175:     if (clash) {
176:       useStore.getState().closeDoc(clash.id);
177:       dropBuffer(clash.id);
178:     }
179:     renameBuffer(current.id, nextId);
180:     useStore.getState().renameDoc(current.id, picked);
181:   }
182: 
183:   // A new file is never written in a legacy encoding (spec 8).
184:   if (isLegacy(current.encoding)) {
185:     useStore.getState().updateDoc(nextId, { encoding: "utf-8", bom: false });
186:   }
187:   useStore.getState().updateDoc(nextId, { readOnly: false, deleted: false });
188: 
189:   const written = await write(nextId, { path: picked, baseHash: null, allowMissing: true });
190:   if (written && previous.id !== nextId) void dropDraft(previous);
191:   return written;
192: }
193:

270: /** Reads the file again and drops it into the buffer as one undo step. */
271: export async function reloadFromDisk(id: string, note = "reloaded from disk"): Promise<void> {
272:   const current = doc(id);
273:   if (!current?.path) return;
274:   try {
275:     const fields = docFields(await readFile(current.path));
276:     useStore.getState().updateDoc(id, fields);
277:     replaceText(id, fields.text);
278:     void dropDraft(current);
279:     useStore.getState().dismissBanner("conflict");
280:     if (note) useStore.getState().setNote(note);
281:   } catch (error) {
282:     useStore.getState().setMessage(`couldn't reload - ${fsError(error).message}`);
283:   }
284: }

294:       const fields = docFields(await readFile(current.path as string, encoding));
295:       useStore.getState().updateDoc(current.id, fields);

297:       useStore.getState().setNote(`reopened as ${encodingLabel(encoding)}`);
298:     } catch (error) {

300:     }

305:     return;
306:   }

310:     actions: [

313:         run: () => {
314:           store.setDialog(null);

316:         },
317:       },

FILE src/app/drafts.ts
1: // %APPDATA%\Plain\drafts\<id>.json - the copy of an edited buffer that
2: // survives a kill (spec 8). Written on a 500 ms debounce and at least once
3: // every 2 s of continuous typing; deleted only when that same text has
4: // reached the disk, or when the user says `don't save`.
5: 
6: import { appDataDir, join } from "@tauri-apps/api/path";
7: import { exists, readDir, readTextFile, remove } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-fs";
8: import { isDirty } from "../editor/buffers";
9: import { normalizeEol, type Eol } from "./eol";
10: import { inTauri } from "./env";
11: import { readFile, trashPath, writeTextAtomic } from "./fs";
12: import { basename, pathKey } from "./paths";
13: import { makeDoc, useStore, type Doc, type Recovery } from "./store";
14: 
15: const FOLDER = "drafts";
16: export const DEBOUNCE_MS = 500;
17: export const MAX_WAIT_MS = 2000;
18: 
19: export interface Draft {
20:   text: string;
21:   path: string | null;
22:   title: string;
23:   baseHash: string | null;
24:   encoding: string;
25:   bom: boolean;
26:   eol: Eol;
27:   finalNewline: boolean;
28:   caret: { line: number; col: number } | null;
29:   savedAt: number;
30: }
31: 
32: /** Short, stable and derived from the path - the same file always lands on
33:  *  the same draft, run after run. */
34: function fnv1a(text: string): string {
35:   let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
36:   for (let index = 0; index < text.length; index += 1) {
37:     hash ^= text.charCodeAt(index);
38:     hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193);
39:   }
40:   return (hash >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, "0");
41: }
42: 
43: export function draftName(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): string {
44:   return `${fnv1a(doc.path ? pathKey(doc.path) : doc.id)}.json`;
45: }
46: 
47: async function draftPath(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): Promise<string> {
48:   return join(await appDataDir(), FOLDER, draftName(doc));
49: }
50: 
51: /* --------------------------------------------------------------- writing */
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Debounce with a ceiling: quiet for 500 ms writes, and typing that never
55:  * pauses still gets written every 2 s (spec 8).
56:  */
57: export function createSchedule(run: () => void): { push: () => void; flush: () => void } {
58:   let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
59:   let firstAt = 0;
60: 
61:   const flush = () => {
62:     clearTimeout(timer);
63:     timer = undefined;
64:     firstAt = 0;
65:     run();
66:   };
67: 
68:   return {
69:     push() {
70:       const now = Date.now();
71:       if (firstAt === 0) firstAt = now;
72:       if (now - firstAt >= MAX_WAIT_MS) {
73:         flush();
74:         return;
75:       }
76:       clearTimeout(timer);
77:       timer = setTimeout(flush, DEBOUNCE_MS);
78:     },
79:     flush,
80:   };
81: }
82: 
83: const pending = new Set<string>();
84: 
85: const schedule = createSchedule(() => {
86:   const ids = [...pending];
87:   pending.clear();
88:   for (const id of ids) void writeDraft(id);
89: });
90: 
91: export function scheduleDraft(id: string): void {
92:   pending.add(id);
93:   schedule.push();
94: }
95: 
96: export function flushDrafts(): void {
97:   schedule.flush();
98: }
99: 
100: /** Tests only. */
101: export function pendingDrafts(): string[] {
102:   return [...pending];
103: }
104: 
105: export async function writeDraft(id: string): Promise<void> {
106:   if (!inTauri) return;
107:   const doc = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
108:   if (!doc || !isDirty(doc.id, doc.text)) return;
109: 
110:   const draft: Draft = {
111:     text: normalizeEol(doc.text),
112:     path: doc.path,
113:     title: doc.title,
114:     baseHash: doc.baseHash,
115:     encoding: doc.encoding,
116:     bom: doc.bom,
117:     eol: doc.eol,
118:     finalNewline: doc.finalNewline,
119:     caret: doc.caret,
120:     savedAt: Date.now(),
121:   };
122:   try {
123:     await writeTextAtomic(await draftPath(doc), JSON.stringify(draft));
124:     useStore.getState().dismissBanner("drafts");
125:   } catch {
126:     // Nothing to offer here: the user cannot fix %APPDATA% from inside the
127:     // app, and the banner has to stay up as long as the risk does (8).
128:     useStore.getState().showBanner({ id: "drafts", text: "can't write recovery draft" });
129:   }
130: }
131: 
132: export async function dropDraft(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): Promise<void> {
133:   if (!inTauri) return;
134:   pending.delete(doc.id);
135:   try {
136:     const file = await draftPath(doc);
137:     if (await exists(file)) await remove(file);
138:   } catch {
139:     /* a draft that will not go away is not worth a banner */
140:   }
141: }
142: 
143: /** Every dirty buffer belongs to the store, so one subscription covers all. */
144: export function installDrafts(): () => void {
145:   return useStore.subscribe((state, previous) => {
146:     if (state.docs === previous.docs) return;
147:     for (const doc of state.docs) {
148:       const before = previous.docs.find((d) => d.id === doc.id);
149:       if (before && before.text === doc.text && before.baseHash === doc.baseHash) continue;
150:       if (isDirty(doc.id, doc.text)) scheduleDraft(doc.id);
151:     }
152:   });
153: }
154: 
155: /* ------------------------------------------------------------ recovering */
156: 
157: async function loadDraft(file: string): Promise<Draft | null> {
158:   try {
159:     const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(await readTextFile(file));
160:     if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object") return null;
161:     const draft = parsed as Draft;
162:     return typeof draft.text === "string" ? draft : null;
163:   } catch {
164:     return null;
165:   }
166: }
167: 
168: /** What the `unsaved work found` screen lists at startup (spec 8). */
169: export async function listDrafts(): Promise<Recovery[]> {
170:   if (!inTauri) return [];
171:   try {
172:     const folder = await join(await appDataDir(), FOLDER);
173:     if (!(await exists(folder))) return [];
174:     const found: Recovery[] = [];
175:     for (const entry of await readDir(folder)) {
176:       if (!entry.isFile || !entry.name.endsWith(".json")) continue;
177:       const file = await join(folder, entry.name);
178:       const draft = await loadDraft(file);
179:       if (!draft) continue;
180:       found.push({
181:         file,
182:         path: draft.path,
183:         title: draft.title || (draft.path ? basename(draft.path) : "Untitled"),
184:         savedAt: draft.savedAt ?? 0,
185:       });
186:     }
187:     return found.sort((a, b) => b.savedAt - a.savedAt);
188:   } catch {
189:     return [];
190:   }
191: }
192: 
193: /**
194:  * Opens the draft as an unsaved document. Says whether the file on disk has
195:  * moved on since - the caller raises the conflict banner, so this module does
196:  * not have to know about banners.
197:  */
198: export async function restoreDraft(entry: Recovery): Promise<{ id: string; conflict: boolean } | null> {
199:   const draft = await loadDraft(entry.file);
200:   if (!draft) return null;
201: 
202:   const text = normalizeEol(draft.text);
203:   let savedText = "";
204:   let readOnly = false;
205:   let deleted = false;
206:   let conflict = false;
207: 
208:   if (draft.path) {
209:     try {
210:       const info = await readFile(draft.path);
211:       savedText = normalizeEol(info.text);
212:       readOnly = info.readOnly;
213:       conflict = info.hash !== draft.baseHash;
214:     } catch {
215:       deleted = true;
216:     }
217:   }
218: 
219:   const id = draft.path ? pathKey(draft.path) : entry.file;
220:   const doc = makeDoc({
221:     id,
222:     path: draft.path,
223:     title: entry.title,
224:     text,
225:     savedText,
226:     dirty: text !== savedText,
227:     mode: "edit",
228:     readOnly,
229:     deleted,
230:     encoding: draft.encoding ?? "utf-8",
231:     bom: draft.bom ?? false,
232:     eol: draft.eol ?? "crlf",
233:     finalNewline: draft.finalNewline ?? false,
234:     baseHash: draft.baseHash ?? null,
235:     caret: draft.caret ?? null,
236:   });
237:   useStore.getState().openDoc(doc);
238:   return { id, conflict };
239: }
240: 
241: /** `discard` goes to the Recycle Bin, not to nowhere (spec 8). */
242: export async function discardDraft(entry: Recovery): Promise<void> {
243:   if (!inTauri) return;
244:   try {
245:     await trashPath(entry.file);
246:   } catch {
247:     try {
248:       await remove(entry.file);
249:     } catch {
250:       /* nothing else to try */
251:     }
252:   }
253: }
FILE src/app/close.ts
1: // Closing a document or the window. Unsaved work is never dropped without
2: // one explicit answer (spec 8).
3: 
4: import { getCurrentWindow } from "@tauri-apps/api/window";
5: import { dropBuffer, flushActiveEditor, isDirty } from "../editor";
6: import { dropDraft } from "./drafts";
7: import { inTauri } from "./env";
8: import { save } from "./save";
9: import { toSession, writeSession } from "./session";
10: import { useStore, type Doc } from "./store";
11: 
12: function unsaved(ids: string[]): Doc[] {
13:   return useStore
14:     .getState()
15:     .docs.filter((d) => ids.includes(d.id) && isDirty(d.id, d.text));
16: }
17: 
18: function forget(ids: string[]): void {
19:   const store = useStore.getState();
20:   for (const id of ids) {
21:     const current = store.docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
22:     if (current) void dropDraft(current);
23:     store.closeDoc(id);
24:     dropBuffer(id);
25:   }
26:   // There is one banner slot and it belonged to a document that is gone.
27:   store.dismissBanner("conflict");
28:   store.dismissBanner("save-failed");
29: }
30: 
31: /**
32:  * Closes the documents, asking once for all of them if any is unsaved.
33:  * `done` runs only when everything really closed - it is how the window
34:  * close request knows it may go through.
35:  */
36: export function closeDocs(ids: string[], done?: () => void): void {
37:   flushActiveEditor();
38:   const store = useStore.getState();
39:   const dirty = unsaved(ids);
40:   if (dirty.length === 0) {
41:     forget(ids);
42:     done?.();
43:     return;
44:   }
45: 
46:   store.setDialog({
47:     title: dirty.length === 1 ? "unsaved changes" : `${dirty.length} files have unsaved changes`,
48:     lines: dirty.map((d) => d.path ?? d.title),
49:     actions: [
50:       {
51:         label: "save",
52:         run: () => {
53:           store.setDialog(null);
54:           void (async () => {
55:             const before = new Set(useStore.getState().docs.map((d) => d.id));
56:             for (const item of dirty) {
57:               // A failed save leaves its own banner up and stops the close.
58:               if (!(await save(item.id))) return;
59:             }
60:             // Save As gave a nameless buffer a new id; it is still the same
61:             // document and it was still asked to close.
62:             const renamed = useStore
63:               .getState()
64:               .docs.filter((d) => !before.has(d.id))
65:               .map((d) => d.id);
66:             forget([...ids, ...renamed]);
67:             done?.();
68:           })();
69:         },
70:       },
71:       {
72:         label: "don't save",
73:         run: () => {
74:           store.setDialog(null);
75:           forget(ids);
76:           done?.();
77:         },
78:       },
79:       { label: "cancel", run: () => store.setDialog(null) },
80:     ],
81:     cancel: () => store.setDialog(null),
82:   });
83: }
84: 
85: export function closeActive(): void {
86:   const { activeId } = useStore.getState();
87:   if (activeId) closeDocs([activeId]);
88: }
89: 
90: /** The window's X and Alt+F4 go through the same one question. */
91: export function installCloseGuard(): () => void {
92:   if (!inTauri) return () => undefined;
93:   let leaving = false;
94:   const window = getCurrentWindow();
95:   const unlisten = window.onCloseRequested((event) => {
96:     if (leaving) return;
97:     event.preventDefault();
98:     const ids = useStore.getState().docs.map((d) => d.id);
99:     // Taken now: closing the documents is what empties the open list, and the
100:     // next launch is supposed to bring them back (spec 6).
101:     const session = toSession();
102:     closeDocs(ids, () => {
103:       leaving = true;
104:       void writeSession(session).then(() => window.destroy());
105:     });
106:   });
107:   return () => void unlisten.then((off) => off());
108: }
FILE src/app/watcher.ts
1: // External changes (spec 8). Rust reports raw paths; only this side knows
2: // the hash a buffer came from, so the whole decision lives here.
3: 
4: import { listen } from "@tauri-apps/api/event";
5: import { isDirty } from "../editor/buffers";
6: import { inTauri } from "./env";
7: import { hashFile, watchPaths } from "./fs";
8: import { pathKey } from "./paths";
9: import { reloadFromDisk, showConflict } from "./save";
10: import { useStore } from "./store";
11: 
12: /** Wave 5 hangs the file tree off this. */
13: export const TREE_CHANGED = "plain:tree-changed";
14: 
15: const checking = new Set<string>();
16: 
17: /**
18:  * Same hash as the last write of ours -> our own change, ignore it.
19:  * Different and the buffer is clean -> reload quietly. Different with edits
20:  * -> the conflict banner, which is the only thing that may lose work.
21:  */
22: export async function checkDoc(id: string): Promise<void> {
23:   if (checking.has(id)) return;
24:   checking.add(id);
25:   try {
26:     const store = useStore.getState();
27:     const doc = store.docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
28:     if (!doc?.path) return;
29: 
30:     const hash = await hashFile(doc.path);
31:     if (hash === null) {
32:       if (!doc.deleted) store.updateDoc(id, { deleted: true });
33:       return;
34:     }
35:     if (doc.deleted) store.updateDoc(id, { deleted: false });
36:     if (hash === doc.baseHash) return;
37:     if (isDirty(id, doc.text)) {
38:       showConflict(id);
39:       return;
40:     }
41:     await reloadFromDisk(id);
42:   } finally {
43:     checking.delete(id);
44:   }
45: }
46: 
47: async function onChange(paths: string[]): Promise<void> {
48:   let tree = false;
49:   for (const path of paths) {
50:     const key = pathKey(path);
51:     const doc = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.path && pathKey(d.path) === key);
52:     if (doc) await checkDoc(doc.id);
53:     else tree = true;
54:   }
55:   if (tree) window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(TREE_CHANGED));
56: }
57: 
58: /** One watcher; changing the library or opening a file restarts it. */
59: let armed = "";
60: 
61: function arm(): void {
62:   const state = useStore.getState();
63:   const files = state.docs.map((d) => d.path).filter((p): p is string => p !== null);
64:   const key = `${state.libraryPath ?? ""}|${files.join("|")}`;
65:   if (key === armed) return;
66:   armed = key;
67:   void watchPaths(state.libraryPath, files).catch(() => undefined);
68: }
69: 
70: export function installWatcher(): () => void {
71:   if (!inTauri) return () => undefined;
72: 
73:   const unsubscribe = useStore.subscribe((state, previous) => {
74:     if (state.docs !== previous.docs || state.libraryPath !== previous.libraryPath) arm();
75:   });
76:   arm();
77: 
78:   const unlisten = listen<{ paths: string[] }>("fs-change", (event) => {
79:     void onChange(event.payload.paths ?? []);
80:   });
81: 
82:   // A file changed while Plain was in the background often produces no event
83:   // at all on network folders, so coming back also checks (spec 8).
84:   const onFocus = () => {
85:     const { activeId } = useStore.getState();
86:     if (activeId) void checkDoc(activeId);
87:   };
88:   window.addEventListener("focus", onFocus);
89: 
90:   return () => {
91:     unsubscribe();
92:     void unlisten.then((off) => off());
93:     window.removeEventListener("focus", onFocus);
94:     // A remount (React strict mode, a hot reload) has to arm it again.
95:     armed = "";
96:   };
97: }
FILE src/app/session.ts
1: // %APPDATA%\Plain\state.json - what was open and where you were in it
2: // (spec 8). Window geometry is not here: the window-state plugin owns it.
3: 
4: import { appDataDir, join } from "@tauri-apps/api/path";
5: import { exists, readTextFile } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-fs";
6: import { inTauri } from "./env";
7: import { writeTextAtomic } from "./fs";
8: import { pathKey } from "./paths";
9: import { useStore, type Mode, type RailView } from "./store";
10: 
11: const FILE = "state.json";
12: const DEBOUNCE_MS = 2000;
13: /** Reading positions are an LRU, not a growing log (spec 8). */
14: export const READING_LIMIT = 300;
15: 
16: export interface SessionFile {
17:   version: 1;
18:   files: { path: string; mode: Mode; caret: { line: number; col: number } | null }[];
19:   active: string | null;
20:   rail: { collapsed: boolean; view: RailView };
21:   library: string | null;
22:   /** Relative paths of the folded folders in the tree (spec 6). */
23:   collapsed: string[];
24:   recent: string[];
25:   /** path -> heading id, oldest first. */
26:   reading: [string, string][];
27: }
28: 
29: /* ----------------------------------------------------- reading positions */
30: 
31: const positions = new Map<string, string>();
32: 
33: /** Read view calls this while scrolling; re-inserting keeps the LRU order. */
34: export function rememberReading(path: string, heading: string): void {
35:   const key = pathKey(path);
36:   if (positions.get(key) === heading) return;
37:   positions.delete(key);
38:   positions.set(key, heading);
39:   while (positions.size > READING_LIMIT) {
40:     const oldest = positions.keys().next();
41:     if (oldest.done) break;
42:     positions.delete(oldest.value);
43:   }
44:   schedule();
45: }
46: 
47: export function readingPosition(path: string): string | null {
48:   return positions.get(pathKey(path)) ?? null;
49: }
50: 
51: /* ------------------------------------------------------------ the file */
52: 
53: export function toSession(): SessionFile {
54:   const state = useStore.getState();
55:   const active = state.docs.find((d) => d.id === state.activeId);
56:   return {
57:     version: 1,
58:     files: state.docs
59:       .filter((d) => d.path !== null)
60:       .map((d) => ({ path: d.path as string, mode: d.mode, caret: d.caret })),
61:     active: active?.path ?? null,
62:     rail: { collapsed: state.railCollapsed, view: state.railView },
63:     library: state.libraryPath,
64:     collapsed: state.collapsed,
65:     recent: state.recent,
66:     reading: [...positions.entries()],
67:   };
68: }
69: 
70: /** Anything unreadable is simply "no session"; a fresh start is not a bug. */
71: export function parseSession(text: string): SessionFile | null {
72:   let raw: unknown;
73:   try {
74:     raw = JSON.parse(text);
75:   } catch {
76:     return null;
77:   }
78:   if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object") return null;
79:   const value = raw as Partial<SessionFile>;
80:   const files = Array.isArray(value.files) ? value.files : [];
81:   const reading = Array.isArray(value.reading) ? value.reading : [];
82:   return {
83:     version: 1,
84:     files: files
85:       .filter((f) => f && typeof f.path === "string")
86:       .map((f) => ({
87:         path: f.path,
88:         mode: f.mode === "edit" ? "edit" : "read",
89:         caret: f.caret && typeof f.caret.line === "number" ? f.caret : null,
90:       })),
91:     active: typeof value.active === "string" ? value.active : null,
92:     rail: {
93:       collapsed: value.rail?.collapsed === true,
94:       view: value.rail?.view === "outline" ? "outline" : "files",
95:     },
96:     library: typeof value.library === "string" ? value.library : null,
97:     collapsed: Array.isArray(value.collapsed)
98:       ? value.collapsed.filter((rel) => typeof rel === "string")
99:       : [],
100:     recent: Array.isArray(value.recent) ? value.recent.filter((p) => typeof p === "string") : [],
101:     reading: reading
102:       .filter((pair) => Array.isArray(pair) && typeof pair[0] === "string" && typeof pair[1] === "string")
103:       .slice(-READING_LIMIT),
104:   };
105: }
106: 
107: export async function loadSession(): Promise<SessionFile | null> {
108:   if (!inTauri) return null;
109:   try {
110:     const file = await join(await appDataDir(), FILE);
111:     if (!(await exists(file))) return null;
112:     const session = parseSession(await readTextFile(file));
113:     if (session) {
114:       positions.clear();
115:       for (const [path, heading] of session.reading) positions.set(path, heading);
116:     }
117:     return session;
118:   } catch {
119:     return null;
120:   }
121: }
122: 
123: /**
124:  * Takes the session it is given, because closing the window empties the open
125:  * list before the app is allowed to go - the snapshot has to be older.
126:  */
127: export async function writeSession(session: SessionFile): Promise<void> {
128:   if (!inTauri) return;
129:   clearTimeout(timer);
130:   timer = undefined;
131:   try {
132:     await writeTextAtomic(await join(await appDataDir(), FILE), JSON.stringify(session));
133:   } catch {
134:     /* losing the session is not worth a banner */
135:   }
136: }
137: 
138: export function flushSession(): Promise<void> {
139:   return writeSession(toSession());
140: }
141: 
142: let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
143: 
144: function schedule(): void {
145:   clearTimeout(timer);
146:   timer = setTimeout(() => void flushSession(), DEBOUNCE_MS);
147: }
148: 
149: /** Everything the session keeps lives in the store, so one watch does it. */
150: export function installSession(): () => void {
151:   return useStore.subscribe((state, previous) => {
152:     if (
153:       state.docs === previous.docs &&
154:       state.activeId === previous.activeId &&
155:       state.railCollapsed === previous.railCollapsed &&
156:       state.railView === previous.railView &&
157:       state.libraryPath === previous.libraryPath &&
158:       state.collapsed === previous.collapsed &&
159:       state.recent === previous.recent
160:     ) {
161:       return;
162:     }
163:     schedule();
164:   });
165: }

FILE src/app/save.ts
1: // Ctrl+S and everything around it (spec 8). The rules, in order:
2: // a clean document is never written; the snapshot that goes to disk is taken
3: // before the write and compared to the buffer after it; the base hash always
4: // follows a successful write; nothing the user did not touch changes.
5: 
6: import { save as saveDialog } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog";
7: import { flushActiveEditor, isDirty, markSaved, renameBuffer, replaceText } from "../editor";
8: import { dropBuffer } from "../editor/buffers";
9: import { dropDraft, writeDraft } from "./drafts";
10: import { inTauri } from "./env";
11: import { encodingLabel, isLegacy, normalizeEol, serialize } from "./eol";
12: import { docFields, fsError, readFile, writeFileAtomic } from "./fs";
13: import { dirname, pathKey } from "./paths";
14: import { activeDoc, useStore, type Doc } from "./store";
15: 
16: /* -------------------------------------------------------------- plumbing */
17: 
18: /**
19:  * Writes of one document never overlap: a second Ctrl+S waits for the first
20:  * (spec 8). Rust serializes writes too; this keeps the store consistent.
21:  */
22: const queues = new Map<string, Promise<unknown>>();
23: 
24: function queued<T>(id: string, run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
25:   const previous = queues.get(id) ?? Promise.resolve();
26:   const next = previous.then(run, run);
27:   queues.set(id, next);
28:   void next.catch(() => undefined).then(() => {
29:     if (queues.get(id) === next) queues.delete(id);
30:   });
31:   return next;
32: }
33: 
34: function doc(id: string): Doc | undefined {
35:   return useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
36: }
37: 
38: /* ------------------------------------------------------------- the write */
39: 
40: /**
41:  * The base hash always follows a successful write, or the next save would
42:  * conflict with our own file (spec 8). Then the buffer is compared to the
43:  * snapshot: unchanged means saved and the draft can go, changed means the
44:  * document is still unsaved and the draft stays with the new base hash.
45:  */
46: function settle(id: string, snapshot: string, hash: string): void {
47:   const store = useStore.getState();
48:   markSaved(id, snapshot);
49:   // Anything typed while the write was in flight counts against the snapshot,
50:   // so the editor is read now rather than on its next idle callback.
51:   flushActiveEditor();
52:   const current = doc(id);
53:   if (!current) return;
54:   const dirty = normalizeEol(current.text) !== snapshot;
55:   store.updateDoc(id, { savedText: snapshot, baseHash: hash, dirty, deleted: false });
56:   store.dismissBanner("conflict");
57:   store.dismissBanner("save-failed");
58:   if (dirty) void writeDraft(id);
59:   else void dropDraft(current);
60: }
61: 
62: interface Target {
63:   path: string;
64:   baseHash: string | null;
65:   allowMissing?: boolean;
66: }
67: 
68: async function write(id: string, target: Target): Promise<boolean> {
69:   const current = doc(id);
70:   if (!current) return false;
71:   const snapshot = normalizeEol(current.text);
72: 
73:   try {
74:     const hash = await writeFileAtomic({
75:       path: target.path,
76:       text: serialize(snapshot, current.eol),
77:       encoding: current.encoding,
78:       bom: current.bom,
79:       eol: current.eol,
80:       baseHash: target.baseHash,
81:       allowMissing: target.allowMissing ?? false,
82:     });
83:     settle(id, snapshot, hash);
84:     // One of the two allowed transformations, and it says so (spec 1.3).
85:     if (current.mixedEol) {
86:       useStore.getState().updateDoc(id, { mixedEol: false });
87:       useStore.getState().setMessage(`line endings normalized to ${current.eol}`);
88:     }
89:     return true;
90:   } catch (error) {
91:     const failure = fsError(error);
92:     if (failure.kind === "conflict") {
93:       showConflict(id);
94:       return false;
95:     }
96:     // Deleted from under us, and the buffer holds edits: put the file back.
97:     if (failure.kind === "missing") {
98:       const back = await write(id, { ...target, allowMissing: true });
99:       if (back) useStore.getState().setNote("recreated");
100:       return back;
101:     }
102:     useStore.getState().showBanner({
103:       id: "save-failed",
104:       text: `couldn't save - ${failure.message}`,
105:       actions: [
106:         { label: "retry", run: () => void save(id) },
107:         { label: "save as:", run: () => void saveAs(id) },
108:       ],
109:     });
110:     return false;
111:   }
112: }
113: 
114: /* ------------------------------------------------------------- commands */
115: 
116: export function saveActive(): Promise<boolean> {
117:   flushActiveEditor();
118:   const current = activeDoc(useStore.getState());
119:   return current ? save(current.id) : Promise.resolve(true);
120: }
121: 
122: /** `Ctrl+S`. Resolves to false when the document is still unsaved. */
123: export function save(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
124:   flushActiveEditor();
125:   return queued(id, async () => {
126:     const current = doc(id);
127:     if (!current) return true;
128:     // A buffer that was never on disk goes through the Save As dialog (6).
129:     if (!current.path) return saveAs(id);
130:     if (current.readOnly) {
131:       useStore.getState().setMessage("read-only - use save as:");
132:       return false;
133:     }
134:     // 8: a clean document is not written at all, and says nothing.
135:     if (!isDirty(id, current.text)) return true;
136:     if (isLegacy(current.encoding)) {
137:       askAboutEncoding(current);
138:       return false;
139:     }
140:     // Deleted from under us: the buffer's edits go back to disk (spec 6).
141:     const recreate = current.deleted;
142:     const written = await write(id, {
143:       path: current.path,
144:       baseHash: current.baseHash,
145:       allowMissing: recreate,
146:     });
147:     if (written && recreate) useStore.getState().setNote("recreated");
148:     return written;
149:   });
150: }
151: 
152: /** `Ctrl+Shift+S`, and the way out of every conflict. */
153: export async function saveAs(id: string): Promise<boolean> {
154:   if (!inTauri) return false;
155:   flushActiveEditor();
156:   const store = useStore.getState();
157:   const current = doc(id);
158:   if (!current) return false;
159: 
160:   const folder = current.path ? dirname(current.path) : store.libraryPath;
161:   const suggestion = current.path ?? (folder ? `${folder}\\${current.title}.md` : `${current.title}.md`);
162:   const extensions = store.settings.library.extensions.map((e) => e.replace(/^\./, ""));
163:   const picked = await saveDialog({
164:     defaultPath: suggestion,
165:     filters: [{ name: "markdown", extensions }],
166:   });
167:   if (typeof picked !== "string") return false;
168: 
169:   const nextId = pathKey(picked);
170:   const previous = { id: current.id, path: current.path };
171: 
172:   if (nextId !== current.id) {
173:     // Saving over a file that is already open would give it two buffers.
174:     const clash = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === nextId);
175:     if (clash) {
176:       useStore.getState().closeDoc(clash.id);
177:       dropBuffer(clash.id);
178:     }
179:     renameBuffer(current.id, nextId);
180:     useStore.getState().renameDoc(current.id, picked);
181:   }
182: 
183:   // A new file is never written in a legacy encoding (spec 8).
184:   if (isLegacy(current.encoding)) {
185:     useStore.getState().updateDoc(nextId, { encoding: "utf-8", bom: false });
186:   }
187:   useStore.getState().updateDoc(nextId, { readOnly: false, deleted: false });
188: 
189:   const written = await write(nextId, { path: picked, baseHash: null, allowMissing: true });
190:   if (written && previous.id !== nextId) void dropDraft(previous);
191:   return written;
192: }

194: /** cp1251 and friends: the one conversion the app is allowed to do (1.3). */

198:     title: `${current.title} is not utf-8`,
199:     lines: [`saving converts it from ${current.encoding} to utf-8.`],
200:     actions: [

202:         label: "convert to utf-8",
203:         run: () => {
204:           store.setDialog(null);
205:           useStore.getState().updateDoc(current.id, { encoding: "utf-8", bom: false });
206:           useStore.getState().setMessage("converted to utf-8");
207:           void save(current.id);
208:         },
209:       },
210:       {
211:         label: "save as:",
212:         run: () => {
213:           store.setDialog(null);
214:           void saveAs(current.id);
215:         },
216:       },
217:       { label: "cancel", run: () => store.setDialog(null) },
218:     ],
219:     cancel: () => store.setDialog(null),
220:   });
221: }

256:     actions: [

258:         label: "reload",
259:         run: () => {
260:           store.setDialog(null);

265:     ],
266:     cancel: () => store.setDialog(null),
267:   });

270: /** Reads the file again and drops it into the buffer as one undo step. */
271: export async function reloadFromDisk(id: string, note = "reloaded from disk"): Promise<void> {
272:   const current = doc(id);
273:   if (!current?.path) return;
274:   try {
275:     const fields = docFields(await readFile(current.path));
276:     useStore.getState().updateDoc(id, fields);
277:     replaceText(id, fields.text);
278:     void dropDraft(current);
279:     useStore.getState().dismissBanner("conflict");
280:     if (note) useStore.getState().setNote(note);
281:   } catch (error) {
282:     useStore.getState().setMessage(`couldn't reload - ${fsError(error).message}`);
283:   }
284: }

305:     return;
306:   }

309:     lines: [`your changes to ${current.title} are lost.`],

314:           store.setDialog(null);

316:         },

FILE src/app/drafts.ts
1: // %APPDATA%\Plain\drafts\<id>.json - the copy of an edited buffer that
2: // survives a kill (spec 8). Written on a 500 ms debounce and at least once
3: // every 2 s of continuous typing; deleted only when that same text has
4: // reached the disk, or when the user says `don't save`.
5: 
6: import { appDataDir, join } from "@tauri-apps/api/path";
7: import { exists, readDir, readTextFile, remove } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-fs";
8: import { isDirty } from "../editor/buffers";
9: import { normalizeEol, type Eol } from "./eol";
10: import { inTauri } from "./env";
11: import { readFile, trashPath, writeTextAtomic } from "./fs";
12: import { basename, pathKey } from "./paths";
13: import { makeDoc, useStore, type Doc, type Recovery } from "./store";
14: 
15: const FOLDER = "drafts";
16: export const DEBOUNCE_MS = 500;
17: export const MAX_WAIT_MS = 2000;
18: 
19: export interface Draft {
20:   text: string;
21:   path: string | null;
22:   title: string;
23:   baseHash: string | null;
24:   encoding: string;
25:   bom: boolean;
26:   eol: Eol;
27:   finalNewline: boolean;
28:   caret: { line: number; col: number } | null;
29:   savedAt: number;
30: }
31: 
32: /** Short, stable and derived from the path - the same file always lands on
33:  *  the same draft, run after run. */
34: function fnv1a(text: string): string {
35:   let hash = 0x811c9dc5;
36:   for (let index = 0; index < text.length; index += 1) {
37:     hash ^= text.charCodeAt(index);
38:     hash = Math.imul(hash, 0x01000193);
39:   }
40:   return (hash >>> 0).toString(16).padStart(8, "0");
41: }
42: 
43: export function draftName(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): string {
44:   return `${fnv1a(doc.path ? pathKey(doc.path) : doc.id)}.json`;
45: }
46: 
47: async function draftPath(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): Promise<string> {
48:   return join(await appDataDir(), FOLDER, draftName(doc));
49: }
50: 
51: /* --------------------------------------------------------------- writing */
52: 
53: /**
54:  * Debounce with a ceiling: quiet for 500 ms writes, and typing that never
55:  * pauses still gets written every 2 s (spec 8).
56:  */
57: export function createSchedule(run: () => void): { push: () => void; flush: () => void } {
58:   let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
59:   let firstAt = 0;
60: 
61:   const flush = () => {
62:     clearTimeout(timer);
63:     timer = undefined;
64:     firstAt = 0;
65:     run();
66:   };
67: 
68:   return {
69:     push() {
70:       const now = Date.now();
71:       if (firstAt === 0) firstAt = now;
72:       if (now - firstAt >= MAX_WAIT_MS) {
73:         flush();
74:         return;
75:       }
76:       clearTimeout(timer);
77:       timer = setTimeout(flush, DEBOUNCE_MS);
78:     },
79:     flush,
80:   };
81: }
82: 
83: const pending = new Set<string>();
84: 
85: const schedule = createSchedule(() => {
86:   const ids = [...pending];
87:   pending.clear();
88:   for (const id of ids) void writeDraft(id);
89: });
90: 
91: export function scheduleDraft(id: string): void {
92:   pending.add(id);
93:   schedule.push();
94: }
95: 
96: export function flushDrafts(): void {
97:   schedule.flush();
98: }
99: 
100: /** Tests only. */
101: export function pendingDrafts(): string[] {
102:   return [...pending];
103: }
104: 
105: export async function writeDraft(id: string): Promise<void> {
106:   if (!inTauri) return;
107:   const doc = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === id);
108:   if (!doc || !isDirty(doc.id, doc.text)) return;
109: 
110:   const draft: Draft = {
111:     text: normalizeEol(doc.text),
112:     path: doc.path,
113:     title: doc.title,
114:     baseHash: doc.baseHash,
115:     encoding: doc.encoding,
116:     bom: doc.bom,
117:     eol: doc.eol,
118:     finalNewline: doc.finalNewline,
119:     caret: doc.caret,
120:     savedAt: Date.now(),
121:   };
122:   try {
123:     await writeTextAtomic(await draftPath(doc), JSON.stringify(draft));
124:     useStore.getState().dismissBanner("drafts");
125:   } catch {
126:     // Nothing to offer here: the user cannot fix %APPDATA% from inside the
127:     // app, and the banner has to stay up as long as the risk does (8).
128:     useStore.getState().showBanner({ id: "drafts", text: "can't write recovery draft" });
129:   }
130: }
131: 
132: export async function dropDraft(doc: Pick<Doc, "id" | "path">): Promise<void> {
133:   if (!inTauri) return;
134:   pending.delete(doc.id);
135:   try {
136:     const file = await draftPath(doc);
137:     if (await exists(file)) await remove(file);
138:   } catch {
139:     /* a draft that will not go away is not worth a banner */
140:   }
141: }
142: 
143: /** Every dirty buffer belongs to the store, so one subscription covers all. */
144: export function installDrafts(): () => void {
145:   return useStore.subscribe((state, previous) => {
146:     if (state.docs === previous.docs) return;
147:     for (const doc of state.docs) {
148:       const before = previous.docs.find((d) => d.id === doc.id);
149:       if (before && before.text === doc.text && before.baseHash === doc.baseHash) continue;
150:       if (isDirty(doc.id, doc.text)) scheduleDraft(doc.id);
151:     }
152:   });
153: }
154: 
155: /* ------------------------------------------------------------ recovering */
156: 
157: async function loadDraft(file: string): Promise<Draft | null> {
158:   try {
159:     const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(await readTextFile(file));
160:     if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== "object") return null;
161:     const draft = parsed as Draft;
162:     return typeof draft.text === "string" ? draft : null;
163:   } catch {
164:     return null;
165:   }
166: }

168: /** What the `unsaved work found` screen lists at startup (spec 8). */
169: export async function listDrafts(): Promise<Recovery[]> {
170:   if (!inTauri) return [];
171:   try {
172:     const folder = await join(await appDataDir(), FOLDER);
173:     if (!(await exists(folder))) return [];
174:     const found: Recovery[] = [];
175:     for (const entry of await readDir(folder)) {
176:       if (!entry.isFile || !entry.name.endsWith(".json")) continue;
177:       const file = await join(folder, entry.name);
178:       const draft = await loadDraft(file);
179:       if (!draft) continue;
180:       found.push({
181:         file,
182:         path: draft.path,
183:         title: draft.title || (draft.path ? basename(draft.path) : "Untitled"),
184:         savedAt: draft.savedAt ?? 0,
185:       });
186:     }
187:     return found.sort((a, b) => b.savedAt - a.savedAt);
188:   } catch {
189:     return [];
190:   }
191: }

193: /**
194:  * Opens the draft as an unsaved document. Says whether the file on disk has
195:  * moved on since - the caller raises the conflict banner, so this module does
196:  * not have to know about banners.
197:  */
198: export async function restoreDraft(entry: Recovery): Promise<{ id: string; conflict: boolean } | null> {
199:   const draft = await loadDraft(entry.file);
200:   if (!draft) return null;
201: 
202:   const text = normalizeEol(draft.text);
203:   let savedText = "";
204:   let readOnly = false;
205:   let deleted = false;
206:   let conflict = false;
207: 
208:   if (draft.path) {
209:     try {
210:       const info = await readFile(draft.path);
211:       savedText = normalizeEol(info.text);
212:       readOnly = info.readOnly;
213:       conflict = info.hash !== draft.baseHash;
214:     } catch {
215:       deleted = true;
216:     }
217:   }
218: 
219:   const id = draft.path ? pathKey(draft.path) : entry.file;
220:   const doc = makeDoc({
221:     id,
222:     path: draft.path,
223:     title: entry.title,
224:     text,
225:     savedText,
226:     dirty: text !== savedText,
227:     mode: "edit",
228:     readOnly,
229:     deleted,
230:     encoding: draft.encoding ?? "utf-8",
231:     bom: draft.bom ?? false,
232:     eol: draft.eol ?? "crlf",
233:     finalNewline: draft.finalNewline ?? false,
234:     baseHash: draft.baseHash ?? null,
235:     caret: draft.caret ?? null,
236:   });
237:   useStore.getState().openDoc(doc);
238:   return { id, conflict };
239: }
240: 
241: /** `discard` goes to the Recycle Bin, not to nowhere (spec 8). */
242: export async function discardDraft(entry: Recovery): Promise<void> {
243:   if (!inTauri) return;
244:   try {
245:     await trashPath(entry.file);
246:   } catch {
247:     try {
248:       await remove(entry.file);
249:     } catch {
250:       /* nothing else to try */
251:     }
252:   }
253: }

1: // Everything that touches the user's files (spec 8). A read reports the
2: // encoding, the BOM and the line endings so a later save can put the bytes
3: // back the way they were; a write goes to a temp file in the same folder and
4: // replaces the original in one step.

19: /// The three cases the front end tells apart: `conflict` stops the save and
20: /// raises a banner, `missing` may be recreated on purpose, `io` is reported.
21: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
22: pub struct FsError {
23:     kind: &'static str,
24:     message: String,
25: }
26: 
27: impl FsError {
28:     fn io(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
29:         Self {
30:             kind: "io",
31:             message: message.into(),
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     fn conflict() -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             kind: "conflict",
38:             message: "file changed on disk".into(),
39:         }
40:     }
41: 
42:     fn missing(path: &Path) -> Self {
43:         Self {
44:             kind: "missing",
45:             message: format!("{} is gone", path.display()),
46:         }
47:     }
48: }
49: 
50: impl From<std::io::Error> for FsError {
51:     fn from(error: std::io::Error) -> Self {
52:         Self::io(error.to_string())
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: pub type FsResult<T> = Result<T, FsError>;
57: 
58: /* --------------------------------------------------------------- reading */
59: 
60: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
61: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
62: pub struct FileInfo {
63:     text: String,
64:     /// encoding_rs label, lowercase: `utf-8`, `utf-16le`, `windows-1251`:
65:     encoding: String,
66:     bom: bool,
67:     /// What the file has: `crlf` `lf` `cr` `mixed` `none`.
68:     eol: String,
69:     /// What a save writes back; `crlf` when the file has no line break yet.
70:     dominant_eol: String,
71:     final_newline: bool,
72:     hash: String,
73:     mtime_ms: f64,
74:     size: u64,
75:     read_only: bool,
76: }
77: 
78: /// A byte-order mark and how many bytes of it to skip.
79: fn bom_of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<(&'static Encoding, usize)> {
80:     if bytes.starts_with(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]) {
81:         Some((UTF_8, 3))
82:     } else if bytes.starts_with(&[0xFF, 0xFE]) {
83:         Some((UTF_16LE, 2))
84:     } else if bytes.starts_with(&[0xFE, 0xFF]) {
85:         Some((UTF_16BE, 2))
86:     } else {
87:         None
88:     }
89: }
90: 
91: /// BOM, then valid UTF-8, then chardetng (spec 8). `forced` comes from
92: /// `reopen as:` and wins over all of it.
93: fn detect(bytes: &[u8], forced: Option<&str>) -> (&'static Encoding, usize) {
94:     if let Some(label) = forced {
95:         let encoding = Encoding::for_label(label.as_bytes()).unwrap_or(UTF_8);
96:         let skip = match bom_of(bytes) {
97:             Some((found, len)) if found == encoding => len,
98:             _ => 0,
99:         };
100:         return (encoding, skip);
101:     }
102:     if let Some(found) = bom_of(bytes) {
103:         return found;
104:     }
105:     if std::str::from_utf8(bytes).is_ok() {
106:         return (UTF_8, 0);
107:     }
108:     // UTF-8 was already ruled out above, so the detector only has to choose
109:     // between the legacy encodings.
110:     let mut detector = EncodingDetector::new(Iso2022JpDetection::Deny);
111:     detector.feed(bytes, true);
112:     (detector.guess(None, Utf8Detection::Deny), 0)
113: }
114: 
115: /// `(what the file has, what a save writes back)`.
116: fn line_endings(text: &str) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
117:     let (mut crlf, mut lf, mut cr) = (0usize, 0usize, 0usize);
118:     let bytes = text.as_bytes();
119:     let mut index = 0;
120:     while index < bytes.len() {
121:         match bytes[index] {
122:             b'\r' => {
123:                 if bytes.get(index + 1) == Some(&b'\n') {
124:                     crlf += 1;
125:                     index += 1;
126:                 } else {
127:                     cr += 1;
128:                 }
129:             }
130:             b'\n' => lf += 1,
131:             _ => {}
132:         }
133:         index += 1;
134:     }
135: 
136:     let kinds = u8::from(crlf > 0) + u8::from(lf > 0) + u8::from(cr > 0);
137:     let dominant = if crlf > 0 && crlf >= lf && crlf >= cr {
138:         "crlf"
139:     } else if lf > 0 && lf >= cr {
140:         "lf"
141:     } else if cr > 0 {
142:         "cr"
143:     } else {
144:         // Nothing to go by: the Windows default (8, files.newFileEol).
145:         "crlf"
146:     };
147:     let eol = match kinds {
148:         0 => "none",
149:         1 => dominant,
150:         _ => "mixed",
151:     };
152:     (eol, dominant)
153: }
154: 
155: fn mtime_ms(meta: &fs::Metadata) -> f64 {
156:     meta.modified()
157:         .ok()
158:         .and_then(|time| time.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
159:         .map(|since| since.as_millis() as f64)
160:         .unwrap_or(0.0)
161: }
162: 
163: /// The text comes back exactly as it is on disk, CRLF and all: CodeMirror
164: /// normalizes it, and the front end keeps `eol` to put it back.
165: pub fn read_info(path: &Path, forced: Option<&str>) -> FsResult<FileInfo> {
166:     let bytes = fs::read(path)?;
167:     let meta = fs::metadata(path)?;
168:     let (encoding, skip) = detect(&bytes, forced);
169:     let (text, _) = encoding.decode_without_bom_handling(&bytes[skip..]);
170:     let (eol, dominant) = line_endings(&text);
171:     Ok(FileInfo {
172:         final_newline: text.ends_with('\n') || text.ends_with('\r'),
173:         eol: eol.into(),
174:         dominant_eol: dominant.into(),
175:         encoding: encoding.name().to_ascii_lowercase(),
176:         bom: skip > 0,
177:         hash: blake3::hash(&bytes).to_hex().to_string(),
178:         mtime_ms: mtime_ms(&meta),
179:         size: meta.len(),
180:         read_only: meta.permissions().readonly(),
181:         text: text.into_owned(),
182:     })
183: }

185: #[tauri::command]
186: pub fn read_file(path: String, encoding: Option<String>) -> FsResult<FileInfo> {
187:     read_info(Path::new(&path), encoding.as_deref())
188: }

199: /// encoding_rs turns the two UTF-16 encodings into UTF-8 on the way out, so
200: /// they are done by hand.
201: fn encode(text: &str, label: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
202:     match label {
203:         "utf-16le" => text.encode_utf16().flat_map(u16::to_le_bytes).collect(),
204:         "utf-16be" => text.encode_utf16().flat_map(u16::to_be_bytes).collect(),
205:         _ => Encoding::for_label(label.as_bytes())
206:             .unwrap_or(UTF_8)
207:             .encode(text)
208:             .0
209:             .into_owned(),
210:     }
211: }
212: 
213: fn bom_bytes(label: &str) -> &'static [u8] {
214:     match label {
215:         "utf-16le" => &[0xFF, 0xFE],
216:         "utf-16be" => &[0xFE, 0xFF],
217:         _ => &[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF],
218:     }
219: }
220: 
221: /// The front end already did this; doing it again keeps a pasted `\n` out of
222: /// a CRLF file. `keep` is for our own files in %APPDATA%.
223: fn apply_eol(text: &str, eol: &str) -> String {
224:     if eol == "keep" {
225:         return text.to_string();
226:     }
227:     let lf = if text.contains('\r') {
228:         text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace('\r', "\n")
229:     } else {
230:         text.to_string()
231:     };
232:     match eol {
233:         "crlf" => lf.replace('\n', "\r\n"),
234:         "cr" => lf.replace('\n', "\r"),
235:         _ => lf,
236:     }
237: }
238: 
239: fn wide(path: &Path) -> Vec<u16> {
240:     path.as_os_str().encode_wide().chain(Some(0)).collect()
241: }
242: 
243: /// temp file in the same folder -> FlushFileBuffers -> ReplaceFileW, which
244: /// keeps the creation time and the attributes of the original (spec 8).
245: fn replace_with(target: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> FsResult<()> {
246:     let dir = target
247:         .parent()
248:         .filter(|parent| !parent.as_os_str().is_empty())
249:         .ok_or_else(|| FsError::io("no parent folder"))?;
250:     fs::create_dir_all(dir)?;
251: 
252:     let mut temp = tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(dir)?;
253:     temp.write_all(bytes)?;
254:     temp.flush()?;
255:     temp.as_file().sync_all()?;
256: 
257:     if target.exists() {
258:         let (file, temp_path) = temp.keep().map_err(|error| FsError::io(error.to_string()))?;
259:         drop(file);
260:         let replaced = wide(target);
261:         let replacement = wide(&temp_path);
262:         let outcome = unsafe {
263:             ReplaceFileW(
264:                 PCWSTR(replaced.as_ptr()),
265:                 PCWSTR(replacement.as_ptr()),
266:                 PCWSTR::null(),
267:                 REPLACEFILE_IGNORE_MERGE_ERRORS,
268:                 None,
269:                 None,
270:             )
271:         };
272:         if let Err(error) = outcome {
273:             let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp_path);
274:             return Err(FsError::io(error.message()));
275:         }
276:     } else {
277:         temp.persist(target)
278:             .map_err(|error| FsError::io(error.error.to_string()))?;
279:     }
280:     Ok(())
281: }

283: #[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
284: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
285: pub struct WriteRequest {
286:     pub path: String,
287:     pub text: String,
288:     pub encoding: String,
289:     pub bom: bool,
290:     pub eol: String,
291:     /// Hash of the bytes the buffer was loaded from; `null` for Save As.
292:     pub base_hash: Option<String>,
293:     /// The file was deleted from under us and the user wants it back (8).
294:     #[serde(default)]
295:     pub allow_missing: bool,
296: }
297: 
298: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
299: pub struct WriteResult {
300:     hash: String,
301: }
302: 
303: /// One lock for every write. A personal editor with one window does not need
304: /// per-path locks, and this also keeps two documents in the same folder from
305: /// racing over their temp files.
306: static WRITE_LOCK: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());
307: 
308: pub fn write_checked(request: &WriteRequest) -> FsResult<String> {
309:     let _guard = WRITE_LOCK.lock().unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
310:     let path = PathBuf::from(&request.path);
311: 
312:     let mut bytes = Vec::new();
313:     if request.bom {
314:         bytes.extend_from_slice(bom_bytes(&request.encoding));
315:     }
316:     bytes.extend_from_slice(&encode(
317:         &apply_eol(&request.text, &request.eol),
318:         &request.encoding,
319:     ));
320: 
321:     if path.exists() {
322:         if let Some(base) = request.base_hash.as_deref() {
323:             let current = blake3::hash(&fs::read(&path)?).to_hex().to_string();
324:             if current != base {
325:                 return Err(FsError::conflict());
326:             }
327:         }
328:     } else if request.base_hash.is_some() && !request.allow_missing {
329:         return Err(FsError::missing(&path));
330:     }
331: 
332:     replace_with(&path, &bytes)?;
333:     Ok(blake3::hash(&bytes).to_hex().to_string())
334: }
335: 
336: #[tauri::command]
337: pub fn write_file_atomic(request: WriteRequest) -> FsResult<WriteResult> {
338:     write_checked(&request).map(|hash| WriteResult { hash })
339: }
340: 
341: /// Drafts and state.json: same temp-and-replace, always UTF-8, never
342: /// touching the line endings of the JSON we produced ourselves.
343: #[tauri::command]
344: pub fn write_text_atomic(path: String, text: String) -> FsResult<()> {
345:     write_checked(&WriteRequest {
346:         path,
347:         text,
348:         encoding: "utf-8".into(),
349:         bom: false,
350:         eol: "keep".into(),
351:         base_hash: None,
352:         allow_missing: true,
353:     })
354:     .map(|_| ())
355: }
356: 
357: /// Recycle Bin, not deletion (spec 6).
358: #[tauri::command]
359: pub fn trash_path(path: String) -> FsResult<()> {
360:     trash::delete(&path).map_err(|error| FsError::io(error.to_string()))
361: }

43:  * disk is a single undo step (spec �8). The new text becomes the clean one.

45: export function replaceText(id: string, text: string): void {
46:   if (live && liveId === id) {
47:     live.dispatch({ changes: { from: 0, to: live.state.doc.length, insert: text } });
48:     keepBuffer(id, live.state, live.scrollDOM.scrollTop);
49:     markSaved(id, text);
50:     // The dispatch queued a sync that would report the document as edited;
51:     // running it now, after the new text is the clean one, settles it.
52:     flushText(live, id);
53:     return;
54:   }
55:   setBufferText(id, text);
56:   markSaved(id, text);
57: }

71: function jump(view: EditorView, line: number): void {
72:   const target = view.state.doc.line(Math.min(Math.max(1, line), view.state.doc.lines));
73:   // Focus first: focusing after the transaction makes the browser scroll to
74:   // where the selection used to be, undoing the jump.
75:   view.focus();
76:   view.dispatch({
77:     selection: { anchor: target.from },

79:   });

82: // The outline and read -> edit send this; it can arrive before the view is
83: // mounted, so it waits here until it is. The listener lives on the module so
84: // it is there before the first mount; the window slot keeps a hot reload from
85: // leaving the previous module's listener (and its dead view) behind.
86: const LISTENER_SLOT = "__plainGotoLine";
87: 
88: if (typeof window !== "undefined") {
89:   const slot = window as unknown as Record<string, EventListener | undefined>;
90:   const previous = slot[LISTENER_SLOT];
91:   if (previous) window.removeEventListener(GOTO_LINE, previous);
92:   const onGotoLine: EventListener = (event) => {
93:     const line = (event as CustomEvent<number>).detail;
94:     if (typeof line !== "number") return;
95:     if (live) jump(live, line);
96:     else pending = { line, at: Date.now() };
97:   };
98:   slot[LISTENER_SLOT] = onGotoLine;
99:   window.addEventListener(GOTO_LINE, onGotoLine);
100: }

102: function takePending(view: EditorView): void {
103:   if (pending && Date.now() - pending.at < PENDING_MS) jump(view, pending.line);
104:   pending = null;

19: /// The three cases the front end tells apart: `conflict` stops the save and
20: /// raises a banner, `missing` may be recreated on purpose, `io` is reported.
21: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
22: pub struct FsError {
23:     kind: &'static str,
24:     message: String,
25: }
26: 
27: impl FsError {
28:     fn io(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
29:         Self {
30:             kind: "io",
31:             message: message.into(),
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     fn conflict() -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             kind: "conflict",
38:             message: "file changed on disk".into(),
39:         }
40:     }
41: 
42:     fn missing(path: &Path) -> Self {
43:         Self {
44:             kind: "missing",
45:             message: format!("{} is gone", path.display()),
46:         }
47:     }
48: }
49: 
50: impl From<std::io::Error> for FsError {
51:     fn from(error: std::io::Error) -> Self {
52:         Self::io(error.to_string())
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: pub type FsResult<T> = Result<T, FsError>;

60: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
61: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
62: pub struct FileInfo {
63:     text: String,
64:     /// encoding_rs label, lowercase: `utf-8`, `utf-16le`, `windows-1251`�?�
65:     encoding: String,
66:     bom: bool,
67:     /// What the file has: `crlf` `lf` `cr` `mixed` `none`.
68:     eol: String,
69:     /// What a save writes back; `crlf` when the file has no line break yet.
70:     dominant_eol: String,
71:     final_newline: bool,
72:     hash: String,
73:     mtime_ms: f64,
74:     size: u64,
75:     read_only: bool,
76: }

78: /// A byte-order mark and how many bytes of it to skip.
79: fn bom_of(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<(&'static Encoding, usize)> {
80:     if bytes.starts_with(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]) {
81:         Some((UTF_8, 3))
82:     } else if bytes.starts_with(&[0xFF, 0xFE]) {
83:         Some((UTF_16LE, 2))
84:     } else if bytes.starts_with(&[0xFE, 0xFF]) {
85:         Some((UTF_16BE, 2))
86:     } else {
87:         None
88:     }
89: }
90: 
91: /// BOM, then valid UTF-8, then chardetng (spec �8). `forced` comes from
92: /// `reopen as�?�` and wins over all of it.
93: fn detect(bytes: &[u8], forced: Option<&str>) -> (&'static Encoding, usize) {
94:     if let Some(label) = forced {
95:         let encoding = Encoding::for_label(label.as_bytes()).unwrap_or(UTF_8);
96:         let skip = match bom_of(bytes) {
97:             Some((found, len)) if found == encoding => len,
98:             _ => 0,
99:         };
100:         return (encoding, skip);
101:     }
102:     if let Some(found) = bom_of(bytes) {
103:         return found;
104:     }
105:     if std::str::from_utf8(bytes).is_ok() {
106:         return (UTF_8, 0);
107:     }
108:     // UTF-8 was already ruled out above, so the detector only has to choose
109:     // between the legacy encodings.
110:     let mut detector = EncodingDetector::new(Iso2022JpDetection::Deny);
111:     detector.feed(bytes, true);
112:     (detector.guess(None, Utf8Detection::Deny), 0)
113: }
114: 
115: /// `(what the file has, what a save writes back)`.
116: fn line_endings(text: &str) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
117:     let (mut crlf, mut lf, mut cr) = (0usize, 0usize, 0usize);
118:     let bytes = text.as_bytes();
119:     let mut index = 0;
120:     while index < bytes.len() {
121:         match bytes[index] {
122:             b'\r' => {
123:                 if bytes.get(index + 1) == Some(&b'\n') {
124:                     crlf += 1;
125:                     index += 1;
126:                 } else {
127:                     cr += 1;
128:                 }
129:             }
130:             b'\n' => lf += 1,
131:             _ => {}
132:         }
133:         index += 1;
134:     }
135: 
136:     let kinds = u8::from(crlf > 0) + u8::from(lf > 0) + u8::from(cr > 0);
137:     let dominant = if crlf > 0 && crlf >= lf && crlf >= cr {
138:         "crlf"
139:     } else if lf > 0 && lf >= cr {
140:         "lf"
141:     } else if cr > 0 {
142:         "cr"
143:     } else {
144:         // Nothing to go by: the Windows default (�8, files.newFileEol).
145:         "crlf"
146:     };
147:     let eol = match kinds {
148:         0 => "none",
149:         1 => dominant,
150:         _ => "mixed",
151:     };
152:     (eol, dominant)
153: }
154: 
155: fn mtime_ms(meta: &fs::Metadata) -> f64 {
156:     meta.modified()
157:         .ok()
158:         .and_then(|time| time.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
159:         .map(|since| since.as_millis() as f64)
160:         .unwrap_or(0.0)
161: }
162: 
163: /// The text comes back exactly as it is on disk, CRLF and all: CodeMirror
164: /// normalizes it, and the front end keeps `eol` to put it back.
165: pub fn read_info(path: &Path, forced: Option<&str>) -> FsResult<FileInfo> {
166:     let bytes = fs::read(path)?;
167:     let meta = fs::metadata(path)?;
168:     let (encoding, skip) = detect(&bytes, forced);
169:     let (text, _) = encoding.decode_without_bom_handling(&bytes[skip..]);
170:     let (eol, dominant) = line_endings(&text);
171:     Ok(FileInfo {
172:         final_newline: text.ends_with('\n') || text.ends_with('\r'),
173:         eol: eol.into(),
174:         dominant_eol: dominant.into(),
175:         encoding: encoding.name().to_ascii_lowercase(),
176:         bom: skip > 0,
177:         hash: blake3::hash(&bytes).to_hex().to_string(),
178:         mtime_ms: mtime_ms(&meta),
179:         size: meta.len(),
180:         read_only: meta.permissions().readonly(),
181:         text: text.into_owned(),
182:     })
183: }

188: }

199: /// encoding_rs turns the two UTF-16 encodings into UTF-8 on the way out, so
200: /// they are done by hand.
201: fn encode(text: &str, label: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
202:     match label {
203:         "utf-16le" => text.encode_utf16().flat_map(u16::to_le_bytes).collect(),
204:         "utf-16be" => text.encode_utf16().flat_map(u16::to_be_bytes).collect(),
205:         _ => Encoding::for_label(label.as_bytes())
206:             .unwrap_or(UTF_8)
207:             .encode(text)
208:             .0
209:             .into_owned(),
210:     }
211: }

1: // Search inside the library (spec �7). One walk, one answer: no index, no

14: /// Per file. A file that matches more than this is not read any further.

37:     line: usize,

63: fn wanted(name: &str, extensions: &[String]) -> bool {
64:     let lower = name.to_lowercase();
65:     extensions.iter().any(|ext| {
66:         let ext = ext.trim_start_matches('.').to_lowercase();
67:         !ext.is_empty() && lower.len() > ext.len() + 1 && lower.ends_with(&format!(".{ext}"))
68:     })
69: }
70: 
71: fn ignored_dir(name: &str) -> bool {
72:     name.starts_with('.') || IGNORED.contains(&name)
73: }
74: 
75: /// A very long line would be a wall of text in a 560px column; the window
76: /// starts at the first match so the match is always on screen.
77: const MAX_LINE: usize = 400;
78: 
79: fn utf16_len(text: &str) -> usize {
80:     text.chars().map(char::len_utf16).sum()
81: }
82: 
83: /// One line of a hit, with the ranges converted from bytes to UTF-16 units.
84: fn line_match(line: usize, text: &str, spans: &[(usize, usize)]) -> LineMatch {
85:     let mut ranges = Vec::with_capacity(spans.len());
86:     for &(from, to) in spans {
87:         let start = utf16_len(&text[..from]);
88:         let end = start + utf16_len(&text[from..to]);
89:         ranges.push([start, end]);
90:     }
91:     let mut text = text.to_string();
92:     if utf16_len(&text) > MAX_LINE {
93:         // Cut the tail only; the offsets in front of it stay correct.
94:         let cut = text
95:             .char_indices()
96:             .map(|(index, _)| index)
97:             .find(|index| utf16_len(&text[..*index]) >= MAX_LINE)
98:             .unwrap_or(text.len());
99:         text.truncate(cut);
100:         text.push('�?�');
101:         ranges.retain(|[_, end]| *end <= MAX_LINE);
102:     }
103:     LineMatch { line, text, ranges }
104: }
105: 
106: /// Everything the walk found, before the caps are applied.
107: fn scan(text: &str, pattern: &regex::Regex) -> (Vec<LineMatch>, bool) {
108:     let mut out = Vec::new();
109:     let mut truncated = false;
110:     for (index, line) in text.lines().enumerate() {
111:         let spans: Vec<(usize, usize)> = pattern
112:             .find_iter(line)
113:             // An empty match (`a*`) would report every position; skip those.
114:             .filter(|m| m.end() > m.start())
115:             .map(|m| (m.start(), m.end()))
116:             .collect();
117:         if spans.is_empty() {
118:             continue;
119:         }
120:         out.push(line_match(index + 1, line, &spans));
121:         if out.len() >= MAX_MATCHES_PER_FILE {
122:             truncated = true;
123:             break;
124:         }
125:     }
126:     (out, truncated)
127: }

129: /// Collects the files to look at. `ignore` does the walking; its gitignore
130: /// handling is off, because the tree does not use it either (spec �6).
131: fn candidates(root: &Path, extensions: &[String]) -> Vec<std::path::PathBuf> {
132:     WalkBuilder::new(root)
133:         .hidden(false)
134:         .ignore(false)
135:         .git_ignore(false)
136:         .git_global(false)
137:         .git_exclude(false)
138:         .parents(false)
139:         .follow_links(false)
140:         .filter_entry(|entry| {
141:             let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
142:             !entry.file_type().is_some_and(|kind| kind.is_dir()) || !ignored_dir(&name)
143:         })
144:         .build()
145:         .filter_map(Result::ok)
146:         .filter(|entry| entry.file_type().is_some_and(|kind| kind.is_file()))
147:         .filter(|entry| wanted(&entry.file_name().to_string_lossy(), extensions))
148:         .map(|entry| entry.into_path())
149:         .collect()
150: }
