152: pub fn search(request: &SearchRequest) -> Result<SearchResponse, String> {
153:     let root = Path::new(&request.root);
154:     if !root.is_dir() {
155:         return Err(format!("not a folder: {}", request.root));
156:     }
157:     if request.query.is_empty() {
158:         return Ok(SearchResponse {
159:             files: Vec::new(),
160:             skipped_large: 0,
161:             truncated: false,
162:         });
163:     }
164: 
165:     let source = if request.regex {
166:         request.query.clone()
167:     } else {
168:         regex::escape(&request.query)
169:     };
170:     let pattern = RegexBuilder::new(&source)
171:         .case_insensitive(!request.case_sensitive)
172:         .build()
173:         .map_err(|error| {
174:             // The multi-line rustc-style message is no use under a text field.
175:             error
176:                 .to_string()
177:                 .lines()
178:                 .last()
179:                 .unwrap_or("invalid regex")
180:                 .trim()
181:                 .to_string()
182:         })?;
183: 
184:     let root_text = root.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
185:     let mut found: Vec<(FileMatches, bool, bool)> = candidates(root, &request.extensions)
186:         .par_iter()
187:         .filter_map(|path| {
188:             let size = std::fs::metadata(path).map(|meta| meta.len()).unwrap_or(0);
189:             if size > LARGE_FILE {
190:                 return Some((
191:                     FileMatches {
192:                         path: path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
193:                         rel: String::new(),
194:                         name: String::new(),
195:                         matches: Vec::new(),
196:                     },
197:                     false,
198:                     true,
199:                 ));
200:             }
201:             let bytes = std::fs::read(path).ok()?;
202:             let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes);
203:             let (matches, truncated) = scan(&text, &pattern);
204:             if matches.is_empty() {
205:                 return None;
206:             }
207:             let full = path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
208:             let rel = full
209:                 .strip_prefix(&root_text)
210:                 .unwrap_or(&full)
211:                 .trim_start_matches(['\\', '/'])
212:                 .replace('\\', "/");
213:             Some((
214:                 FileMatches {
215:                     name: path
216:                         .file_name()
217:                         .map(|name| name.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
218:                         .unwrap_or_default(),
219:                     path: full,
220:                     rel,
221:                     matches,
222:                 },
223:                 truncated,
224:                 false,
225:             ))
226:         })
227:         .collect();
228: 
229:     let skipped_large = found.iter().filter(|(_, _, large)| *large).count();
230:     found.retain(|(_, _, large)| !*large);
231:     let mut truncated = found.iter().any(|(_, cut, _)| *cut);
232: 
233:     let mut files: Vec<FileMatches> = found.into_iter().map(|(file, _, _)| file).collect();
234:     files.sort_by(|a, b| crate::tree::natural_cmp(&a.rel, &b.rel));
235: 
236:     // The global cap: whole files are dropped rather than half-shown.
237:     let mut lines = 0;
238:     let mut kept = Vec::new();
239:     for file in files {
240:         if lines >= MAX_LINES {
241:             truncated = true;
242:             break;
243:         }
244:         lines += file.matches.len();
245:         kept.push(file);
246:     }
247: 
248:     Ok(SearchResponse {
249:         files: kept,
250:         skipped_large,
251:         truncated,
252:     })
253: }
254: 
255: #[tauri::command]
256: pub fn search_folder(request: SearchRequest) -> Result<SearchResponse, String> {
257:     search(&request)
258: }

FILE src-tauri/src/tree.rs
1: // The library tree (spec �6). One recursive read of the folder, sorted the
2: // way a person expects: folders first, then natural order. No metadata is
3: // collected �?" the tree only knows names.
4: 
5: use std::cmp::Ordering;
6: use std::fs;
7: use std::path::Path;
8: 
9: use serde::Serialize;
10: 
11: /// Deep enough for any notes folder; a loop of junctions cannot run away.
12: const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 24;
13: 
14: /// Folders nobody wants in a notes tree (spec �6).
15: const IGNORED: [&str; 3] = [".git", ".obsidian", "node_modules"];
16: 
17: #[derive(Debug, Serialize)]
18: #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
19: pub struct Node {
20:     name: String,
21:     /// Absolute path, spelled the way this platform spells it.
22:     path: String,
23:     /// Path relative to the root, always `/` separated �?" the row's identity.
24:     rel: String,
25:     dir: bool,
26:     children: Vec<Node>,
27: }
28: 
29: fn ignored_dir(name: &str) -> bool {
30:     name.starts_with('.') || IGNORED.contains(&name)
31: }
32: 
33: /// `.md` with or without the dot, in any case.
34: fn wanted(name: &str, extensions: &[String]) -> bool {
35:     let lower = name.to_lowercase();
36:     extensions.iter().any(|ext| {
37:         let ext = ext.trim_start_matches('.').to_lowercase();
38:         !ext.is_empty() && lower.len() > ext.len() + 1 && lower.ends_with(&format!(".{ext}"))
39:     })
40: }
41: 
42: /// One piece of a name: a run of digits or a run of everything else.
43: #[derive(PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
44: enum Chunk {
45:     Num(u128),
46:     Text(String),
47: }
48: 
49: fn chunks(name: &str) -> Vec<Chunk> {
50:     let mut out = Vec::new();
51:     let mut rest = name;
52:     while !rest.is_empty() {
53:         let digits = rest.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit());
54:         let end = rest
55:             .find(|c: char| c.is_ascii_digit() != digits)
56:             .unwrap_or(rest.len());
57:         let (head, tail) = rest.split_at(end);
58:         out.push(match head.parse::<u128>() {
59:             Ok(value) if digits => Chunk::Num(value),
60:             // A number too long for u128 sorts as the text it is.
61:             _ => Chunk::Text(head.to_lowercase()),
62:         });
63:         rest = tail;
64:     }
65:     out
66: }
67: 
68: /// `a2.md` before `a10.md`, case ignored; identical names keep a stable order.
69: pub fn natural_cmp(a: &str, b: &str) -> Ordering {
70:     chunks(a).cmp(&chunks(b)).then_with(|| a.cmp(b))
71: }
72: 
73: fn read_dir(dir: &Path, prefix: &str, extensions: &[String], depth: usize) -> Vec<Node> {
74:     let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) else {
75:         return Vec::new();
76:     };
77: 
78:     let mut folders: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
79:     let mut files: Vec<Node> = Vec::new();
80: 
81:     for entry in entries.flatten() {
82:         let Ok(kind) = entry.file_type() else { continue };
83:         // Symlinks and junctions are not followed (spec �6).
84:         if kind.is_symlink() {
85:             continue;
86:         }
87:         let name = entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
88:         let rel = if prefix.is_empty() {
89:             name.clone()
90:         } else {
91:             format!("{prefix}/{name}")
92:         };
93:         let path = entry.path();
94: 
95:         if kind.is_dir() {
96:             if ignored_dir(&name) {
97:                 continue;
98:             }
99:             let children = if depth + 1 < MAX_DEPTH {
100:                 read_dir(&path, &rel, extensions, depth + 1)
101:             } else {
102:                 Vec::new()
103:             };
104:             folders.push(Node {
105:                 name,
106:                 path: path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
107:                 rel,
108:                 dir: true,
109:                 children,
110:             });
111:         } else if kind.is_file() && wanted(&name, extensions) {
112:             files.push(Node {
113:                 name,
114:                 path: path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
115:                 rel,
116:                 dir: false,
117:                 children: Vec::new(),
118:             });
119:         }
120:     }
121: 
122:     folders.sort_by(|a, b| natural_cmp(&a.name, &b.name));
123:     files.sort_by(|a, b| natural_cmp(&a.name, &b.name));
124:     folders.extend(files);
125:     folders
126: }
127: 
128: /// The whole tree in one call. An unreadable sub-folder is simply empty.
129: #[tauri::command]
130: pub fn read_tree(root: String, extensions: Vec<String>) -> Result<Vec<Node>, String> {
131:     let dir = Path::new(&root);
132:     if !dir.is_dir() {
133:         return Err(format!("not a folder: {root}"));
134:     }
135:     Ok(read_dir(dir, "", &extensions, 0))
136: }
137: 
138: /// `file`, `dir` or `missing` �?" what a dropped or argument path turned out
139: /// to be (spec �6).
140: #[tauri::command]
141: pub fn path_kind(path: String) -> String {
142:     let path = Path::new(&path);
143:     if path.is_dir() {
144:         "dir".into()
145:     } else if path.is_file() {
146:         "file".into()
147:     } else {
148:         "missing".into()
149:     }
150: }
151: 
152: /// `rename` in the tree: the file keeps its bytes and gets a new name (�6).
153: #[tauri::command]
154: pub fn rename_path(from: String, to: String) -> Result<(), String> {
155:     if Path::new(&to).exists() {
156:         return Err(format!("{to} already exists"));
157:     }
158:     fs::rename(&from, &to).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
159: }
160: 
161: /// `new folder` in the tree.
162: #[tauri::command]
163: pub fn create_dir(path: String) -> Result<(), String> {
164:     if Path::new(&path).exists() {
165:         return Err(format!("{path} already exists"));
166:     }
167:     fs::create_dir_all(&path).map_err(|error| error.to_string())
168: }

1: // The Windows menu bar (spec �4). It has no markup of its own: every entry
2: // is a command out of the registry, so a title written there shows up here.
3: // Rebuilt whenever something it displays changes �?" the recent list, the
4: // theme, the check marks �?" because a native menu has no data binding.
5: 
6: import { Menu, MenuItem, PredefinedMenuItem, Submenu, CheckMenuItem } from "@tauri-apps/api/menu";
7: import { getCurrentWindow } from "@tauri-apps/api/window";
8: import { parseChord } from "./chords";

17: /**
18:  * Real Windows accelerators work and were measured not to fire a second time
19:  * on top of the app's own keydown (`Ctrl+B`, `Ctrl+Shift+D` each applied
20:  * once), but Windows renders them in its own `Ctrl+Shift+K` capitals, which
21:  * is not the microcopy this app speaks (spec �1.4) �?" and `Ctrl+=`/`-`/`0`
22:  * belong to WebView2, which we must not race. So the chord goes into the
23:  * label after a tab, which Windows right-aligns, and the app keeps every key.
24:  */
25: const ACCELERATORS = false;
26: 
27: /** Last ten of the twenty the session keeps (spec �4). */
28: const RECENT_IN_MENU = 10;
29: 
30: /** "Ctrl+Shift+S" -> "ctrl shift s", the way the spec writes chords. */
31: function chordText(chord: string): string {
32:   return chord
33:     .split("+")
34:     .map((part) => part.trim().toLowerCase())
35:     .join(" ");
36: }
37: 
38: /** muda parses the key part as a KeyboardEvent.code, which chords.ts makes. */
39: function accelerator(chord: string): string | undefined {
40:   if (!ACCELERATORS) return undefined;
41:   const parsed = parseChord(chord);
42:   const parts: string[] = [];
43:   if (parsed.ctrl) parts.push("Control");
44:   if (parsed.alt) parts.push("Alt");
45:   if (parsed.shift) parts.push("Shift");
46:   parts.push(parsed.code);
47:   return parts.join("+");
48: }
49: 
50: interface EntryOptions {
51:   /** Overrides the command's own title. */
52:   text?: string;
53:   enabled?: boolean;
54: }
55: 
56: /** One registry command as a menu item, chord and all. */
57: function entry(id: string, options: EntryOptions = {}) {
58:   const found = command(id);
59:   const chord = found?.chord ?? found?.hint;
60:   const label = options.text ?? found?.title ?? id;
61:   return MenuItem.new({
62:     id: `plain:${id}`,
63:     text: chord && !ACCELERATORS ? `${label}\t${chordText(chord)}` : label,
64:     enabled: options.enabled ?? true,
65:     accelerator: chord ? accelerator(chord) : undefined,
66:     action: () => runCommand(id),
67:   });
68: }
69: 
70: function separator() {
71:   return PredefinedMenuItem.new({ item: "Separator" });
72: }
73: 
74: /** A tick that behaves like a radio button: the theme, one of three. */
75: function check(id: string, text: string, checked: boolean, run: () => void) {
76:   return CheckMenuItem.new({ id: `plain:${id}`, text, checked, action: run });
77: }

79: async function fileMenu(): Promise<Submenu> {

108:           await MenuItem.new({ text: "utf-16", action: () => reopenAs("utf-16le") }),
109:         ],
110:       }),
111:       await separator(),
112:       await entry("file.close"),
113:       await entry("file.exit"),
114:     ],
115:   });

195: async function build(): Promise<Menu> {
196:   return Menu.new({
197:     items: [await fileMenu(), await editMenu(), await viewMenu(), await helpMenu()],
198:   });

200: 
201: /** One rebuild at a time, and the newest state always wins. */
202: let building = false;
203: let again = false;
204: 
205: async function refresh(): Promise<void> {
206:   if (building) {
207:     again = true;
208:     return;
209:   }
210:   building = true;
211:   try {
212:     const menu = await build();
213:     const previous = await menu.setAsWindowMenu(getCurrentWindow());
214:     // Every rebuild makes a new set of Rust-side resources; the old menu is
215:     // off the window and nothing points at it any more.
216:     if (previous) await previous.close();
217:   } catch (error) {
218:     console.error("couldn't build the menu", error);
219:   } finally {
220:     building = false;
221:     if (again) {
222:       again = false;
223:       void refresh();
224:     }
225:   }
226: }
227: 
228: /** What the menu displays; a change in any of it means a rebuild. */
229: function signature(): string {
230:   const state = useStore.getState();
231:   return [
232:     state.theme,
233:     String(state.alwaysOnTop),
234:     String(lineNumbersOn()),
235:     state.recent.slice(0, RECENT_IN_MENU).join("|"),
236:   ].join("␀");
237: }
238: 
239: export function installMenu(): () => void {
240:   if (!inTauri) return () => undefined;
241: 
242:   let last = signature();
243:   void refresh();
244: 
245:   const onChange = () => {
246:     const next = signature();
247:     if (next === last) return;
248:     last = next;
249:     void refresh();
250:   };
251: 
252:   const offStore = useStore.subscribe(onChange);
253:   const offNumbers = onLineNumbers(onChange);
254:   return () => {
255:     offStore();
256:     offNumbers();
257:   };
258: }
FILE src/editor/remote.ts
1: // Find, replace and `go to line` are app commands (spec �12), so their chords
2: // live in the registry and the editor only answers the events. Without this
3: // the same chord would be handled twice: once by CodeMirror, once by the app.
4: 
5: import { findNext, findPrevious, gotoLine, openSearchPanel } from "@codemirror/search";
6: import type { Extension } from "@codemirror/state";
7: import { ViewPlugin } from "@codemirror/view";
8: import { FIND, FIND_STEP, GOTO_LINE_PROMPT, REPLACE } from "../read/events";
9: import { openReplace } from "./findPanel";
10: 
11: export const remoteCommands: Extension = ViewPlugin.define((view) => {
12:   const find = () => openSearchPanel(view);
13:   const replace = () => openReplace(view);
14:   const step = (event: Event) => {
15:     const direction = (event as CustomEvent<1 | -1>).detail;
16:     if (direction < 0) findPrevious(view);
17:     else findNext(view);
18:   };
19:   const goto = () => gotoLine(view);
20: 
21:   window.addEventListener(FIND, find);
22:   window.addEventListener(REPLACE, replace);
23:   window.addEventListener(FIND_STEP, step);
24:   window.addEventListener(GOTO_LINE_PROMPT, goto);
25: 
26:   return {
27:     destroy() {
28:       window.removeEventListener(FIND, find);
29:       window.removeEventListener(REPLACE, replace);
30:       window.removeEventListener(FIND_STEP, step);
31:       window.removeEventListener(GOTO_LINE_PROMPT, goto);
32:     },
33:   };
34: });
FILE src/editor/keymap.ts
1: // CodeMirror matches key bindings by `key`, which breaks every letter chord
2: // in a Russian layout (spec �12). Our commands go through this thin layer
3: // instead: same chord spelling as the app, matched by KeyboardEvent.code.
4: 
5: import {
6:   deleteLine,
7:   indentLess,
8:   indentMore,
9:   redo,
10:   selectAll,
11:   undo,
12: } from "@codemirror/commands";
13: import { foldCode, unfoldCode } from "@codemirror/language";
14: import { selectNextOccurrence } from "@codemirror/search";
15: import type { Extension } from "@codemirror/state";
16: import { ViewPlugin, type Command } from "@codemirror/view";
17: import { matchesChord, parseChord } from "../app/chords";
18: import {
19:   cycleList,
20:   insertLink,
21:   tabIndent,
22:   toggleBold,
23:   toggleCheckbox,
24:   toggleCodeBlock,
25:   toggleHeading,
26:   toggleInlineCode,
27:   toggleItalic,
28:   toggleQuote,
29: } from "./commands";
30: 
31: export interface CodeBinding {
32:   chord: string;
33:   run: Command;
34: }
35: 
36: /**
37:  * Runs the first binding whose physical chord matches. This listens on the
38:  * editor in the capture phase rather than through CodeMirror's own keydown
39:  * handling, because the app swallows Ctrl+F/Ctrl+G with preventDefault on
40:  * window (spec �12) and CodeMirror skips its handlers once that is set.
41:  */
42: export function codeKeymap(bindings: CodeBinding[]): Extension {
43:   const compiled = bindings.map((b) => ({ chord: parseChord(b.chord), run: b.run }));
44:   return ViewPlugin.define((view) => {
45:     const onKeydown = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
46:       if (event.isComposing) return;
47:       // The find panel has its own keys.
48:       if ((event.target as HTMLElement | null)?.closest(".cm-panels")) return;
49:       for (const binding of compiled) {
50:         if (!matchesChord(binding.chord, event)) continue;
51:         if (binding.run(view)) event.preventDefault();
52:         return;
53:       }
54:     };
55:     view.dom.addEventListener("keydown", onKeydown, true);
56:     return { destroy: () => view.dom.removeEventListener("keydown", onKeydown, true) };
57:   });
58: }
59: 
60: /** Chords the app layer owns; CodeMirror must keep its hands off them. */
61: const yieldToApp: Command = () => true;
62: 
63: export function editorKeymap(): Extension {
64:   return codeKeymap([
65:     // formatting (�5.2)
66:     { chord: "Ctrl+B", run: toggleBold },
67:     { chord: "Ctrl+I", run: toggleItalic },
68:     { chord: "Ctrl+E", run: toggleInlineCode },
69:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+`", run: toggleCodeBlock },
70:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+K", run: insertLink },
71:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+Q", run: toggleQuote },
72:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+L", run: cycleList },
73:     { chord: "Ctrl+Enter", run: toggleCheckbox },
74:     { chord: "Ctrl+1", run: toggleHeading(1) },
75:     { chord: "Ctrl+2", run: toggleHeading(2) },
76:     { chord: "Ctrl+3", run: toggleHeading(3) },
77:     { chord: "Ctrl+4", run: toggleHeading(4) },
78:     { chord: "Ctrl+5", run: toggleHeading(5) },
79:     { chord: "Ctrl+6", run: toggleHeading(6) },
80:     { chord: "Ctrl+]", run: indentMore },
81:     { chord: "Ctrl+[", run: indentLess },
82:     { chord: "Tab", run: tabIndent },
83:     { chord: "Shift+Tab", run: indentLess },
84: 
85:     // editing (�12)
86:     { chord: "Ctrl+Z", run: undo },
87:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+Z", run: redo },
88:     { chord: "Ctrl+Y", run: redo },
89:     { chord: "Ctrl+A", run: selectAll },
90:     { chord: "Ctrl+D", run: selectNextOccurrence },
91:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+X", run: deleteLine },
92:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+[", run: foldCode },
93:     { chord: "Ctrl+Shift+]", run: unfoldCode },
94: 
95:     // Find, replace and go-to-line are app commands now: the registry owns
96:     // their chords and remote.ts answers the events (spec �12).
97: 
98:     // Ctrl+/ is the app's read/edit switch, not CodeMirror's comment toggle.
99:     { chord: "Ctrl+/", run: yieldToApp },
100:   ]);
101: }
FILE src/app/keys.ts
1: // One keyboard layer for the whole app. There are no chords here: every
2: // binding comes from the command registry (spec �12), so a shortcut and the
3: // menu entry that shows it can never drift apart. Tree keys (`F2`, `Delete`,
4: // the arrows) are local to the tree and live in the rail.
5: 
6: import { tinykeys } from "tinykeys";
7: import { chordToPattern, matchesChord } from "./chords";
8: import { commands } from "./registry";
9: 
10: /**
11:  * WebView2 keeps its own accelerators (spec �12 leaves them on for zoom), but
12:  * these must not reach it �?" they are ours, or they would reload or print.
13:  */
14: const SWALLOW = [
15:   "Ctrl+F",
16:   "Ctrl+P",
17:   "Ctrl+G",
18:   "F5",
19:   "Ctrl+S",
20:   "Ctrl+Shift+S",
21:   "Ctrl+N",
22:   "Ctrl+O",
23:   "Ctrl+H",
24:   "Ctrl+K",
25: ];
26: 
27: /** chord -> action, straight out of the registry. */
28: export function bindings(): Record<string, () => void> {
29:   const map: Record<string, () => void> = {};
30:   for (const command of commands) {
31:     if (!command.chord) continue;
32:     map[command.chord] = () => void command.run();
33:   }
34:   return map;
35: }
36: 
37: export function installKeys(): () => void {
38:   const swallow = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
39:     if (SWALLOW.some((chord) => matchesChord(chord, event))) event.preventDefault();
40:   };
41:   window.addEventListener("keydown", swallow, { capture: true });
42: 
43:   // WebView2 would otherwise show its own context menu (spec �12). Bubble
44:   // phase, so an element that has its own menu can stop this first.
45:   const noMenu = (event: MouseEvent) => event.preventDefault();
46:   window.addEventListener("contextmenu", noMenu);
47: 
48:   const map: Record<string, (event: KeyboardEvent) => void> = {};
49:   for (const [chord, run] of Object.entries(bindings())) {
50:     map[chordToPattern(chord)] = (event) => {
51:       event.preventDefault();
52:       run();
53:     };
54:   }
55: 
56:   const off = tinykeys(window, map, {
57:     // Shortcuts must keep working while the editor (contenteditable) has

90: export function parseSettings(text: string): ParsedSettings {
91:   if (text.trim() === "") return { settings: DEFAULTS, invalid: false };
92:   let raw: unknown;

94:     raw = JSON.parse(text);
95:   } catch {

99:     return { settings: DEFAULTS, invalid: true };
100:   }
101:   return { settings: normalizeSettings(raw), invalid: false };
102: }

24: }

26: const BUTTONS: Button[] = [
27:   { label: "B", title: "bold", className: "tb-bold", run: toggleBold },
28:   { label: "I", title: "italic", className: "tb-italic", run: toggleItalic },
29:   { label: "S", title: "strikethrough", className: "tb-strike", run: toggleStrike },
30:   { label: "`", title: "code", className: "tb-code", run: toggleInlineCode },

33: ];

35: /** `link` and `quote` sit behind the separator, as in the mockup. */
36: const SEPARATOR_BEFORE = 4;
37: 
38: class FormatToolbar {
39:   private dom: HTMLElement | null = null;
40:   /** Only the newest pending mouseup may place the panel. */
41:   private token = 0;
42:   /** A click on a button ends in a mouseup that must not bring it back. */
43:   private suppress = false;
44: 
45:   constructor(private view: EditorView) {
46:     view.dom.addEventListener("mouseup", this.onMouseUp);
47:     view.scrollDOM.addEventListener("scroll", this.hide);
48:     view.dom.addEventListener("focusout", this.onFocusOut);
49:   }
50: 
51:   update(update: ViewUpdate): void {
52:     // Typing, moving the caret and dragging a selection all take it away;
53:     // the mouseup that ends a drag is what brings it back.
54:     if (update.docChanged || update.selectionSet || update.focusChanged) this.hide();
55:   }
56: 
57:   destroy(): void {
58:     this.view.dom.removeEventListener("mouseup", this.onMouseUp);
59:     this.view.scrollDOM.removeEventListener("scroll", this.hide);
60:     this.view.dom.removeEventListener("focusout", this.onFocusOut);
61:     this.hide();
62:   }
63: 
64:   private onFocusOut = (event: FocusEvent): void => {
65:     // Clicking a button moves the focus inside the panel; that is not a blur.
66:     const next = event.relatedTarget;
67:     if (next instanceof Node && this.dom?.contains(next)) return;
68:     this.hide();
69:   };
70: 
71:   // CodeMirror settles the selection in its own mouseup handler, so the panel
72:   // is placed one task later, when the selection is the final one.
73:   private onMouseUp = (): void => {
74:     if (this.suppress) {
75:       this.suppress = false;
76:       return;
77:     }
78:     const token = ++this.token;
79:     window.setTimeout(() => {
80:       if (token === this.token) this.show();
81:     }, 0);
82:   };
83: 
84:   private hide = (): void => {
85:     this.token += 1;
86:     this.dom?.remove();
87:     this.dom = null;
88:   };
89: 
90:   private build(): HTMLElement {
91:     const dom = document.createElement("div");
92:     dom.className = "format-toolbar";
93:     BUTTONS.forEach((button, index) => {
94:       if (index === SEPARATOR_BEFORE) {
95:         const separator = document.createElement("span");
96:         separator.className = "tb-sep";
97:         dom.append(separator);
98:       }
99:       const element = document.createElement("button");
100:       if (button.className) element.className = button.className;
101:       element.title = button.title;
102:       element.textContent = button.label;
103:       // mousedown, not click: the default would take the selection away
104:       // before the command has anything to work on.
105:       element.addEventListener("mousedown", (event) => {
106:         event.preventDefault();
107:         this.suppress = true;
108:         this.hide();
109:         button.run(this.view);
110:         this.view.focus();
111:       });
112:       dom.append(element);
113:     });
114:     return dom;
115:   }
116: 
117:   private show(): void {
118:     const { main } = this.view.state.selection;
119:     if (main.empty || !this.view.hasFocus) return;
120: 
121:     const coords = this.view.coordsAtPos(main.from);
122:     if (!coords) return;
123: 
124:     const dom = this.dom ?? this.build();
125:     if (!dom.isConnected) this.view.dom.append(dom);
126:     this.dom = dom;
127: 
128:     // coordsAtPos is in client space; the panel is absolute inside .cm-editor.
129:     const host = this.view.dom.getBoundingClientRect();
130:     const left = Math.min(
131:       Math.max(0, coords.left - host.left),
132:       Math.max(0, host.width - dom.offsetWidth),
133:     );
134:     dom.style.left = `${Math.round(left)}px`;
135:     dom.style.top = `${Math.round(coords.top - host.top - OFFSET)}px`;
136:   }
137: }

14: /// Paths waiting for the frontend to collect them: launch arguments and
15: /// whatever a second launch handed over.
16: #[derive(Default)]
17: struct PendingPaths(Mutex<Vec<String>>);
18: 
19: /// The same, for folders: a folder given as an argument opens as the library
20: /// (spec �6).
21: #[derive(Default)]
22: struct PendingFolders(Mutex<Vec<String>>);
23: 
24: /// argv -> absolute paths. A relative argument belongs to the working
25: /// directory of the process that produced it, which for a second launch is
26: /// not our own, so the cwd is always passed in. Only arguments that really
27: /// are files survive: `tauri dev` passes `--color always`, and dropping
28: /// anything that starts with `-` would still leave `always` behind.
29: fn resolved_args<I: IntoIterator<Item = String>>(argv: I, cwd: &Path) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
30:     argv.into_iter()
31:         .skip(1)
32:         .map(|arg| {
33:             let path = PathBuf::from(arg);
34:             let absolute = if path.is_absolute() {
35:                 path
36:             } else {
37:                 cwd.join(path)
38:             };
39:             // Drops the "." components a shell leaves behind.
40:             absolute.components().collect()
41:         })
42:         .collect()
43: }
44: 
45: fn path_args<I: IntoIterator<Item = String>>(argv: I, cwd: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
46:     resolved_args(argv, cwd)
47:         .into_iter()
48:         .filter(|path| path.is_file())
49:         .map(|path| path.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
50:         .collect()
51: }
52: 
53: /// A folder argument is a library, not a document (spec �6).
54: fn folder_args<I: IntoIterator<Item = String>>(argv: I, cwd: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
55:     resolved_args(argv, cwd)
56:         .into_iter()
57:         .filter(|path| path.is_dir())
58:         .map(|path| path.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
59:         .collect()
60: }
61: 
62: /// Widens the fs scope �?" the dialog plugin only covers what the user picked
63: /// in a dialog �?" and parks the paths until the frontend asks for them.
64: fn queue_paths<R: Runtime, M: Manager<R>>(manager: &M, paths: Vec<String>) {
65:     if paths.is_empty() {
66:         return;
67:     }
68:     if let Some(scope) = manager.try_fs_scope() {
69:         for path in &paths {
70:             let _ = scope.allow_file(path);
71:         }
72:     }
73:     if let Ok(mut queue) = manager.state::<PendingPaths>().0.lock() {
74:         queue.extend(paths);
75:     }
76: }
77: 
78: /// Parks folder arguments the same way, and widens the scope they need.
79: fn queue_folders<R: Runtime, M: Manager<R>>(manager: &M, folders: Vec<String>) {
80:     if folders.is_empty() {
81:         return;
82:     }
83:     if let Some(scope) = manager.try_fs_scope() {
84:         for folder in &folders {
85:             let _ = scope.allow_directory(folder, true);
86:         }
87:     }
88:     if let Ok(mut queue) = manager.state::<PendingFolders>().0.lock() {
89:         queue.extend(folders);
90:     }
91: }
92: 
93: /// Drained by the frontend at startup and again on every `open-path` signal,
94: /// so a path that arrives before the listener exists is never lost.
95: #[tauri::command]
96: fn take_pending_paths(pending: State<'_, PendingPaths>) -> Vec<String> {
97:     pending
98:         .0
99:         .lock()
100:         .map(|mut queue| std::mem::take(&mut *queue))
101:         .unwrap_or_default()
102: }
103: 
104: #[tauri::command]
105: fn take_pending_folders(pending: State<'_, PendingFolders>) -> Vec<String> {
106:     pending
107:         .0
108:         .lock()
109:         .map(|mut queue| std::mem::take(&mut *queue))
110:         .unwrap_or_default()
111: }
112: 
113: /// Hands a folder to the asset protocol so its images can be shown, and to
114: /// the file-system scope so links inside it can be opened (spec �9).
115: /// Called by the frontend for the folder of the open file, for the library,
116: /// and for whatever an `outside folder �� allow` placeholder points at.
117: #[tauri::command]
118: fn allow_asset_dir(app: tauri::AppHandle, path: String) -> Result<(), String> {
119:     let dir = Path::new(&path);
120:     if !dir.is_dir() {
121:         return Err(format!("not a folder: {path}"));
122:     }
123:     app.asset_protocol_scope()
124:         .allow_directory(dir, true)
125:         .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
126:     if let Some(scope) = app.try_fs_scope() {
127:         scope
128:             .allow_directory(dir, true)
129:             .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
130:     }
131:     Ok(())
132: }

134: /// The webview never leaves our own origin (spec �14); links open in the
135: /// system browser instead.
136: fn navigation_guard<R: Runtime>() -> TauriPlugin<R> {
137:     PluginBuilder::new("plain-navigation")
138:         .on_navigation(|_webview, url: &Url| match url.scheme() {
139:             "tauri" => url.host_str() == Some("localhost"),
140:             "http" => {
141:                 url.host_str() == Some("tauri.localhost")
142:                     || (cfg!(dev) && url.host_str() == Some("localhost"))
143:             }
144:             _ => false,
145:         })
146:         .build()
147: }
148: 
149: pub fn run() {
150:     tauri::Builder::default()
151:         // Order matters: single-instance first (spec �13), and persisted-scope
152:         // reads the fs scope during its own setup, so fs has to come before it.
153:         .plugin(tauri_plugin_single_instance::init(|app, argv, cwd| {
154:             if let Some(window) = app.get_webview_window("main") {
155:                 let _ = window.unminimize();
156:                 let _ = window.show();
157:                 let _ = window.set_focus();
158:             }
159:             let cwd = Path::new(&cwd);
160:             let paths = path_args(argv.clone(), cwd);
161:             let folders = folder_args(argv, cwd);
162:             if !paths.is_empty() || !folders.is_empty() {
163:                 queue_paths(app, paths);
164:                 queue_folders(app, folders);
165:                 // No payload: the event only says "there is something to take".
166:                 let _ = app.emit("open-path", ());

FILE src-tauri/src/watch.rs
1: // One debounced watcher for the library root and for the folders of files
2: // that are open outside it (spec �6). Whatever it sees goes to the front end
3: // as a single `fs-change` event; deciding what a change means is the front
4: // end's job, because only it knows the hash the buffer came from.
5: 
6: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
7: use std::sync::Mutex;
8: use std::time::Duration;
9: 
10: use notify::{RecommendedWatcher, RecursiveMode};
11: use notify_debouncer_full::{new_debouncer, DebounceEventResult, Debouncer, RecommendedCache};
12: use serde::Serialize;
13: use tauri::{AppHandle, Emitter, State};
14: 
15: #[derive(Default)]
16: pub struct Watcher(Mutex<Option<Debouncer<RecommendedWatcher, RecommendedCache>>>);
17: 
18: #[derive(Clone, Serialize)]
19: struct Change {
20:     paths: Vec<String>,
21: }
22: 
23: /// `.git`, `.obsidian`, `node_modules`, dot-folders �?" and, usefully, the
24: /// `.tmp�?�` file our own atomic write leaves for a millisecond.
25: fn ignored(path: &Path) -> bool {
26:     path.components().any(|component| {
27:         let name = component.as_os_str().to_string_lossy();
28:         name == "node_modules" || (name.starts_with('.') && name != "." && name != "..")
29:     })
30: }
31: 
32: fn same_root(folder: &Path, root: &str) -> bool {
33:     folder
34:         .to_string_lossy()
35:         .to_lowercase()
36:         .starts_with(&root.to_lowercase())
37: }
38: 
39: /// Restarts the watcher over the given root and files. Called again whenever
40: /// the library or the set of open documents changes.
41: #[tauri::command]
42: pub fn watch(
43:     app: AppHandle,
44:     root: Option<String>,
45:     files: Vec<String>,
46:     state: State<'_, Watcher>,
47: ) -> Result<(), String> {
48:     let mut slot = state.0.lock().map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
49:     // Dropping the old one stops its thread; there is only ever one.
50:     *slot = None;
51: 
52:     let handle = app.clone();
53:     let mut debouncer = new_debouncer(
54:         Duration::from_millis(150),
55:         None,
56:         move |result: DebounceEventResult| {
57:             let Ok(events) = result else { return };
58:             let mut paths: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
59:             for event in events {
60:                 for path in &event.paths {
61:                     if ignored(path) {
62:                         continue;
63:                     }
64:                     let text = path.to_string_lossy().into_owned();
65:                     if !paths.contains(&text) {
66:                         paths.push(text);
67:                     }
68:                 }
69:             }
70:             if !paths.is_empty() {
71:                 let _ = handle.emit("fs-change", Change { paths });
72:             }
73:         },
74:     )
75:     .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
76: 
77:     if let Some(root) = root.as_deref() {
78:         let path = Path::new(root);
79:         if path.is_dir() {
80:             debouncer
81:                 .watch(path, RecursiveMode::Recursive)
82:                 .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
83:         }
84:     }
85: 
86:     let mut folders: Vec<PathBuf> = Vec::new();
87:     for file in &files {
88:         let Some(folder) = Path::new(file).parent() else {
89:             continue;
90:         };
91:         if !folder.is_dir() {
92:             continue;
93:         }
94:         if root.as_deref().is_some_and(|root| same_root(folder, root)) {
95:             continue;
96:         }
97:         if !folders.iter().any(|seen| seen == folder) {
98:             folders.push(folder.to_path_buf());
99:         }
100:     }
101:     for folder in folders {
102:         debouncer
103:             .watch(&folder, RecursiveMode::NonRecursive)
104:             .map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
105:     }
106: 
107:     *slot = Some(debouncer);
108:     Ok(())
109: }
110: 
111: #[tauri::command]
112: pub fn unwatch(state: State<'_, Watcher>) -> Result<(), String> {
113:     let mut slot = state.0.lock().map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
114:     *slot = None;
115:     Ok(())
116: }

15: /** The names already used in that folder, so a new one can dodge them. */
16: export function siblings(parent: string): string[] {
17:   const state = useStore.getState();
18:   if (state.libraryPath && pathKey(state.libraryPath) === pathKey(parent)) {
19:     return state.tree.map((node) => node.name);
20:   }
21:   const node = nodeAt(state.tree, parent);
22:   return node?.children.map((child) => child.name) ?? [];
23: }

26: export function suggestedName(parent: string, kind: "file" | "folder"): string {
27:   const extension = useStore.getState().settings.library.extensions[0] ?? ".md";
28:   const wanted = kind === "file" ? `Untitled${extension}` : "New folder";
29:   return uniqueName(wanted, siblings(parent));

36: /**
37:  * `new file`: an empty file, written the same atomic way as any save, then
38:  * opened in edit (spec �6).
39:  */
40: export async function createFile(parent: string, typed: string): Promise<void> {
41:   const store = useStore.getState();
42:   const problem = nameError(typed);
43:   if (problem) {
44:     store.setMessage(problem);
45:     return;
46:   }
47:   const extension = store.settings.library.extensions[0] ?? ".md";
48:   const name = uniqueName(withExtension(typed.trim(), extension), siblings(parent));
49:   const path = joinPath(parent, name);
50:   try {
51:     await writeFileAtomic({
52:       path,
53:       text: "",
54:       encoding: "utf-8",
55:       bom: false,
56:       eol: store.settings.files.newFileEol,
57:       baseHash: null,
58:       allowMissing: true,
59:     });
60:     await reloadTree();
61:     if (await openPaths([path])) useStore.getState().setMode("edit");
62:     useStore.getState().setTreeSelected(path);
63:   } catch (error) {
64:     complain(error, "create the file");
65:   }
66: }

87:  * An open document follows its file, buffer and all.

89: export async function renameEntry(from: string, typed: string): Promise<void> {
90:   const problem = nameError(typed);
91:   if (problem) {
92:     useStore.getState().setMessage(problem);
93:     return;
94:   }
95:   const name = typed.trim();
96:   if (name === basename(from)) return;
97:   const to = joinPath(dirname(from), name);
98:   try {

101:     if (open) {

103:       renameBuffer(open.id, next);
104:       useStore.getState().renameDoc(open.id, to);
105:     }
106:     await reloadTree();
107:     useStore.getState().setTreeSelected(to);
108:   } catch (error) {
109:     complain(error, "rename");
110:   }
111: }

113: /** Everything the tree knows about is either a file or a folder of them. */
114: function openUnder(path: string): { id: string; path: string | null }[] {
115:   const key = pathKey(path);
116:   return useStore
117:     .getState()
118:     .docs.filter((doc) => {
119:       if (!doc.path) return false;
120:       const own = pathKey(doc.path);
121:       return own === key || own.startsWith(`${key}/`);
122:     })
123:     .map((doc) => ({ id: doc.id, path: doc.path }));
124: }

146: async function remove(path: string): Promise<void> {
147:   const affected = openUnder(path);
148:   try {
149:     if (inTauri) await trashPath(path);
150:   } catch (error) {
151:     complain(error, "delete");
152:     return;
153:   }
154:   // The file is gone on purpose, so its buffer and its draft go with it.
155:   const store = useStore.getState();
156:   for (const doc of affected) {
157:     void dropDraft(doc);
158:     store.closeDoc(doc.id);
159:     dropBuffer(doc.id);
160:   }
161:   if (pathKey(store.treeSelected ?? "") === pathKey(path)) store.setTreeSelected(null);
162:   await reloadTree();
163:   store.setMessage("moved to the recycle bin");
164: }
FILE src/library/tree.ts
1: // The library tree (spec �6). Rust reads and sorts the folder; this side
2: // only decides what is on screen, and reloads when the watcher says the
3: // folder changed.
4: 
5: import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";
6: import { inTauri } from "../app/env";
7: import { useStore, type TreeNode } from "../app/store";
8: import { TREE_CHANGED } from "../app/watcher";
9: 
10: /** A tree change is often a burst of events; one reload is enough. */
11: const RELOAD_MS = 300;
12: 
13: /** One row of the rendered tree; folders carry a header, files a name. */
14: export interface Row {
15:   node: TreeNode;
16:   /** 0 at the root of the library. */
17:   depth: number;
18:   collapsed: boolean;
19: }
20: 
21: /**
22:  * Depth-first, skipping what is folded shut. Folders come first because Rust
23:  * sorted them that way (spec �6); nothing is re-ordered here.
24:  */
25: export function flatten(nodes: TreeNode[], collapsed: Set<string>, depth = 0): Row[] {
26:   const rows: Row[] = [];
27:   for (const node of nodes) {
28:     const shut = node.dir && collapsed.has(node.rel);
29:     rows.push({ node, depth, collapsed: shut });
30:     if (node.dir && !shut) rows.push(...flatten(node.children, collapsed, depth + 1));
31:   }
32:   return rows;
33: }
34: 
35: /** Every file in the tree, deepest last �?" what quick search searches. */
36: export function files(nodes: TreeNode[]): TreeNode[] {
37:   const out: TreeNode[] = [];
38:   const walk = (list: TreeNode[]) => {
39:     for (const node of list) {
40:       if (node.dir) walk(node.children);
41:       else out.push(node);
42:     }
43:   };
44:   walk(nodes);
45:   return out;
46: }
47: 
48: /** Finds a node by its absolute path; used to keep the selection alive. */
49: export function nodeAt(nodes: TreeNode[], path: string): TreeNode | null {
50:   const key = path.toLowerCase();
51:   const walk = (list: TreeNode[]): TreeNode | null => {
52:     for (const node of list) {
53:       if (node.path.toLowerCase() === key) return node;
54:       const found = node.dir ? walk(node.children) : null;
55:       if (found) return found;
56:     }
57:     return null;
58:   };
59:   return walk(nodes);
60: }
61: 
62: /** Windows spelling, and it keeps whatever separator the parent used. */
63: export function joinPath(parent: string, name: string): string {
64:   const separator = parent.includes("\\") || !parent.includes("/") ? "\\" : "/";
65:   return `${parent.replace(/[\\/]+$/, "")}${separator}${name}`;
66: }
67: 
68: export async function readTree(root: string, extensions: string[]): Promise<TreeNode[]> {
69:   return invoke<TreeNode[]>("read_tree", { root, extensions });
70: }
71: 
72: /** `file`, `dir` or `missing` �?" what a dropped path turned out to be. */
73: export async function pathKind(path: string): Promise<string> {
74:   if (!inTauri) return "missing";
75:   return invoke<string>("path_kind", { path });
76: }
77: 
78: let loading: Promise<void> | null = null;
79: 
80: /** Reads the tree again. Failures leave the previous tree alone. */
81: export async function reloadTree(): Promise<void> {
82:   if (loading) return loading;
83:   const store = useStore.getState();
84:   const root = store.libraryPath;
85:   if (!root || !inTauri) {
86:     store.setTree([]);
87:     return;
88:   }
89:   loading = (async () => {
90:     try {
91:       const tree = await readTree(root, store.settings.library.extensions);
92:       // The library may have changed under the await.
93:       if (useStore.getState().libraryPath === root) useStore.getState().setTree(tree);
94:     } catch {
95:       useStore.getState().setMessage("couldn't read the library folder");
96:     } finally {
97:       loading = null;
98:     }
99:   })();
100:   return loading;
101: }
102: 
103: /**
104:  * Keeps the tree in step with the library and with the disk. The watcher is
105:  * already running over the library root (spec �6); this only listens.
106:  */
107: export function installTree(): () => void {
108:   let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
109:   const later = () => {
110:     clearTimeout(timer);
111:     timer = setTimeout(() => void reloadTree(), RELOAD_MS);
112:   };
113: 
114:   const unsubscribe = useStore.subscribe((state, previous) => {
115:     if (
116:       state.libraryPath !== previous.libraryPath ||
117:       state.settings.library.extensions !== previous.settings.library.extensions
118:     ) {
119:       void reloadTree();
120:     }
121:   });
122: 
123:   window.addEventListener(TREE_CHANGED, later);
124:   void reloadTree();
125: 
126:   return () => {
127:     clearTimeout(timer);
128:     unsubscribe();
129:     window.removeEventListener(TREE_CHANGED, later);
130:   };
131: }

1: // Search inside the library (spec �7). Rust answers a whole request at once;
2: // this side debounces the typing and throws away answers to questions that
3: // are no longer being asked.
4: 
5: import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";
6: import { inTauri } from "../app/env";
7: 
8: export interface LineMatch {
9:   /** 1-based, so it can go straight to `plain:goto-line`. */
10:   line: number;
11:   text: string;
12:   /** `[from, to]` pairs, in UTF-16 units. */
13:   ranges: [number, number][];
14: }
15: 
16: export interface FileMatches {
17:   path: string;
18:   rel: string;
19:   name: string;
20:   matches: LineMatch[];
21: }
22: 
23: export interface SearchAnswer {
24:   files: FileMatches[];
25:   skippedLarge: number;
26:   truncated: boolean;
27: }
28: 
29: export interface SearchQuery {
30:   root: string;
31:   query: string;
32:   caseSensitive: boolean;
33:   regex: boolean;
34:   extensions: string[];
35: }
36: 
37: export const DEBOUNCE_MS = 250;
38: 
39: export function searchFolder(request: SearchQuery): Promise<SearchAnswer> {
40:   return invoke<SearchAnswer>("search_folder", { request });
41: }
42: 
43: export interface Runner {
44:   /** Asks again after the debounce; the caller gets one answer or one error. */
45:   run: (request: SearchQuery) => void;
46:   /** Drops whatever is in flight �?" used when the screen goes away. */
47:   stop: () => void;
48: }
49: 
50: /**
51:  * One search at a time from the user's point of view: a newer question
52:  * cancels the older answer, which is what the counter is for (spec �7).
53:  */
54: export function runner(
55:   onAnswer: (answer: SearchAnswer) => void,
56:   onError: (message: string) => void,
57: ): Runner {
58:   let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
59:   let issued = 0;
60: 
61:   const stop = () => {
62:     clearTimeout(timer);
63:     issued += 1;
64:   };
65: 
66:   return {
67:     stop,
68:     run: (request) => {
69:       clearTimeout(timer);
70:       issued += 1;
71:       const mine = issued;
72:       if (request.query.trim() === "" || !inTauri) {
73:         onAnswer({ files: [], skippedLarge: 0, truncated: false });
74:         return;
75:       }
76:       timer = setTimeout(() => {
77:         void searchFolder(request)
78:           .then((answer) => {
79:             if (mine === issued) onAnswer(answer);
80:           })
81:           .catch((error: unknown) => {
82:             if (mine !== issued) return;
83:             onError(typeof error === "string" ? error : String(error));
84:           });
85:       }, DEBOUNCE_MS);
86:     },
87:   };

FILE src/library/dnd.ts
1: // Dropping on the window (spec �6): a file opens, a folder becomes the
2: // library. Tauri hands over the paths; only the kind has to be asked for.
3: 
4: import { getCurrentWebview } from "@tauri-apps/api/webview";
5: import { openLibraryPath, openPaths } from "../app/commands";
6: import { inTauri } from "../app/env";
7: import { useStore } from "../app/store";
8: import { pathKind } from "./tree";
9: 
10: async function accept(paths: string[]): Promise<void> {
11:   const files: string[] = [];
12:   let folder: string | null = null;
13:   for (const path of paths) {
14:     const kind = await pathKind(path);
15:     if (kind === "dir") folder ??= path;
16:     else if (kind === "file") files.push(path);
17:   }
18:   // The library first, so files dropped with it land inside a known root.
19:   if (folder) await openLibraryPath(folder);
20:   if (files.length > 0 && (await openPaths(files)) && !folder) {
21:     useStore.getState().setRailCollapsed(true);
22:   }
23: }
24: 
25: export function installDrop(): () => void {
26:   if (!inTauri) return () => undefined;
27:   const unlisten = getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent((event) => {
28:     if (event.payload.type !== "drop") return;
29:     void accept(event.payload.paths ?? []);
30:   });
31:   return () => void unlisten.then((off) => off());
32: }

FILE src/app/fs.ts
1: // The Rust side of the file system (src-tauri/src/fs.rs), typed. Everything
2: // that reads or writes a user file goes through here �?" plugin-fs is only used
3: // for our own folder in %APPDATA%.
4: 
5: import { invoke } from "@tauri-apps/api/core";
6: import { normalizeEol, type Eol } from "./eol";
7: import { LARGE_TEXT, useStore, type Doc } from "./store";
8: 
9: export interface FileInfo {
10:   text: string;
11:   encoding: string;
12:   bom: boolean;
13:   /** What the file has; `mixed` and `none` are not valid to write back. */
14:   eol: Eol | "mixed" | "none";
15:   dominantEol: Eol;
16:   finalNewline: boolean;
17:   hash: string;
18:   mtimeMs: number;
19:   size: number;
20:   readOnly: boolean;
21: }
22: 
23: export interface WriteRequest {
24:   path: string;
25:   text: string;
26:   encoding: string;
27:   bom: boolean;
28:   eol: Eol;
29:   baseHash: string | null;
30:   allowMissing?: boolean;
31: }
32: 
33: export interface FsError {
34:   kind: "conflict" | "missing" | "io";
35:   message: string;
36: }
37: 
38: /** Rust rejects with the serialized error; anything else is an io failure. */
39: export function fsError(error: unknown): FsError {
40:   if (error && typeof error === "object" && "kind" in error && "message" in error) {
41:     return error as FsError;
42:   }
43:   return { kind: "io", message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) };
44: }
45: 
46: /** `encoding` forces one instead of detecting it (`reopen as�?�`, spec �8). */
47: export function readFile(path: string, encoding?: string): Promise<FileInfo> {
48:   return invoke<FileInfo>("read_file", { path, encoding: encoding ?? null });
49: }
50: 
51: export async function writeFileAtomic(request: WriteRequest): Promise<string> {
52:   const { hash } = await invoke<{ hash: string }>("write_file_atomic", {
53:     request: { allowMissing: false, ...request },
54:   });
55:   return hash;
56: }
57: 
58: /** null when the file is not there. */
59: export function hashFile(path: string): Promise<string | null> {
60:   return invoke<string | null>("hash_file", { path });
61: }
62: 
63: /** Our own files in %APPDATA%: same temp-and-replace, always UTF-8. */
64: export function writeTextAtomic(path: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
65:   return invoke("write_text_atomic", { path, text });
66: }
67: 
68: /** Recycle Bin, not deletion (spec �6). */
69: export function trashPath(path: string): Promise<void> {
70:   return invoke("trash_path", { path });
71: }
72: 
73: export function watchPaths(root: string | null, files: string[]): Promise<void> {
74:   return invoke("watch", { root, files });
75: }
76: 
77: /**
78:  * The document fields a freshly read file decides. Used when opening, when
79:  * reloading after an external change and after `reopen as�?�`.
80:  */
81: export function docFields(
82:   info: FileInfo,
83: ): Pick<
84:   Doc,
85:   | "text"
86:   | "savedText"
87:   | "encoding"
88:   | "bom"
89:   | "eol"
90:   | "mixedEol"
91:   | "finalNewline"
92:   | "baseHash"
93:   | "readOnly"
94:   | "large"
95:   | "deleted"
96:   | "dirty"
97: > {
98:   const text = normalizeEol(info.text);
99:   return {
100:     text,
101:     savedText: text,
102:     encoding: info.encoding,
103:     bom: info.bom,
104:     // A file with no line break yet has no style of its own (spec �8).
105:     eol: info.eol === "none" ? useStore.getState().settings.files.newFileEol : info.dominantEol,
106:     mixedEol: info.eol === "mixed",
107:     finalNewline: info.finalNewline,
108:     baseHash: info.hash,
109:     readOnly: info.readOnly,
110:     large: info.size > LARGE_TEXT,
111:     deleted: false,
112:     dirty: false,
113:   };
114: }

1: // Everything a shortcut, a menu or a link can trigger. Saving lives in
2: // save.ts and closing in close.ts; the rest is here.

11: import { inTauri } from "./env";
12: import { docFields, fsError, hashFile, readFile, writeTextAtomic } from "./fs";
13: import { basename, pathKey } from "./paths";

18: /**
19:  * Reads each path into the open list; the first one becomes active.
20:  * Returns whether anything ended up open.
21:  */
22: export async function openPaths(paths: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
23:   const { activate, openDoc, showBanner } = useStore.getState();
24:   let opened = false;
25: 
26:   for (const path of paths) {
27:     // Already open under another spelling of the same path: just show it,
28:     // and do not read the file a second time.
29:     const existing = useStore.getState().docs.find((d) => d.id === pathKey(path));
30:     if (existing) {
31:       activate(existing.id);
32:       opened = true;
33:       continue;
34:     }
35:     try {
36:       openDoc(makeDoc({ id: pathKey(path), path, ...docFields(await readFile(path)) }));
37:       opened = true;
38:     } catch (error) {
39:       showBanner({
40:         id: "open-failed",
41:         text: `couldn't open ${basename(path)} �?" ${fsError(error).message}`,
42:         actions: [{ label: "dismiss", run: () => useStore.getState().dismissBanner("open-failed") }],
43:       });
44:     }
45:   }
46:   return opened;
47: }

49: /**
50:  * `Ctrl+N`. With a library open the tree grows a row with an inline name
51:  * field in the root folder; without one it is a nameless buffer whose
52:  * `Ctrl+S` is Save As (spec �6).
53:  */
54: let untitled = 0;

56: export function newDoc(): void {
57:   const store = useStore.getState();
58:   if (store.libraryPath) {
59:     store.setRailCollapsed(false);
60:     store.setRailView("files");
61:     store.setTreeDraft({ parent: store.libraryPath, kind: "file" });
62:     return;
63:   }
64:   untitled += 1;
65:   store.openDoc(
66:     makeDoc({
67:       id: `untitled-${untitled}`,
68:       path: null,
69:       text: "",
70:       mode: "edit",
71:       eol: store.settings.files.newFileEol,
72:     }),
73:   );
74: }

76: /** `F5`: build the document again, and re-read it when it is clean. */
77: export function refresh(): void {
78:   const doc = activeDoc(useStore.getState());
79:   if (!doc?.path) {
80:     emitRerender();
81:     return;
82:   }
83:   if (isDirty(doc.id, doc.text)) {
84:     useStore.getState().setMessage("unsaved changes �?" save or reload from banner");
85:     emitRerender();
86:     return;
87:   }
88:   void reloadFromDisk(doc.id, "").then(emitRerender);
89: }

104: export async function drainPendingPaths(): Promise<void> {
105:   const folders = await pendingFolders();
106:   const first = folders[0];
107:   if (first) await openLibraryPath(first);
108:   const paths = await pendingPaths();
109:   if (paths.length === 0) return;
110:   // A file on its own arrives with the rail out of the way; a file that came
111:   // with its folder does not, because the folder is the point.
112:   if ((await openPaths(paths)) && !first) useStore.getState().setRailCollapsed(true);
113: }

1: // Search inside the library (spec �7): a screen in the style of the library
2: // instead of the document. One Rust call per question, results grouped by
3: // file, a click lands on the line in edit.
4: 
5: import { useEffect, useMemo, useRef, useState } from "react";
6: import { openInEdit } from "../app/commands";
7: import { basename } from "../app/paths";
8: import { emitGotoLine } from "../read/events";
9: import { useStore } from "../app/store";
10: import { runner, type LineMatch, type SearchAnswer } from "../library/search";
11: import "./library.css";
12: 
13: /** `notes/ideas.md` -> `notes`; a file in the root has nothing to add. */
14: function folderOf(rel: string): string {
15:   const at = rel.lastIndexOf("/");
16:   return at < 0 ? "" : rel.slice(0, at);
17: }
18: 
19: /** The matched parts of a context line, painted with the accent. */
20: function Line({ match }: { match: LineMatch }) {
21:   const parts: React.ReactNode[] = [];
22:   let at = 0;
23:   match.ranges.forEach(([from, to], index) => {
24:     if (from > at) parts.push(match.text.slice(at, from));
25:     parts.push(<mark key={index}>{match.text.slice(from, to)}</mark>);
26:     at = to;
27:   });
28:   if (at < match.text.length) parts.push(match.text.slice(at));
29:   return <span className="folder-search-text">{parts}</span>;
30: }
31: 
32: export function FolderSearch() {
33:   const libraryPath = useStore((s) => s.libraryPath);
34:   const extensions = useStore((s) => s.settings.library.extensions);
35: 
36:   const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
37:   const [caseSensitive, setCaseSensitive] = useState(false);
38:   const [regex, setRegex] = useState(false);
39:   const [answer, setAnswer] = useState<SearchAnswer | null>(null);
40:   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
41:   const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
42: 
43:   const ask = useMemo(
44:     () =>
45:       runner(
46:         (result) => {
47:           setError(null);
48:           setAnswer(result);
49:         },
50:         (message) => {
51:           setError(message);
52:           setAnswer(null);
53:         },
54:       ),
55:     [],
56:   );
57: 
58:   useEffect(() => () => ask.stop(), [ask]);
59:   useEffect(() => input.current?.focus(), []);
60: 
61:   // `Esc` goes back to the document from anywhere on the screen (spec �7).
62:   useEffect(() => {
63:     const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent) => {
64:       if (event.key !== "Escape") return;
65:       event.preventDefault();
66:       useStore.getState().setFolderSearch(false);
67:     };
68:     window.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
69:     return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
70:   }, []);
71: 
72:   useEffect(() => {
73:     if (!libraryPath) return;
74:     ask.run({ root: libraryPath, query, caseSensitive, regex, extensions });
75:   }, [ask, libraryPath, query, caseSensitive, regex, extensions]);
76: 
77:   const close = () => useStore.getState().setFolderSearch(false);
78: 
79:   const lines = answer?.files.reduce((total, file) => total + file.matches.length, 0) ?? 0;
80: 
81:   const note = (): string | null => {
82:     if (error) return error;
83:     if (query.trim() === "") return null;
84:     if (!answer) return null;
85:     const parts = [
86:       lines === 0
87:         ? "no matches"
88:         : `${lines} ${lines === 1 ? "line" : "lines"} in ${answer.files.length} ${
89:             answer.files.length === 1 ? "file" : "files"
90:           }`,
91:     ];
92:     if (answer.truncated) parts.push("showing the first of them");
93:     if (answer.skippedLarge > 0) {
94:       parts.push(`${answer.skippedLarge} files over 2 mb skipped`);
95:     }
96:     return parts.join(" �� ");
97:   };
98: 
99:   return (
100:     <div className="folder-search">
101:       <h1 className="folder-search-title">
102:         search in <span className="is-where">{basename(libraryPath ?? "")}</span>
103:       </h1>
104: 
105:       <div className="folder-search-field">
106:         <span className="qs-glyph">�?</span>
107:         <input
108:           ref={input}
109:           className="folder-search-input"
110:           value={query}
111:           placeholder="find in files"
112:           spellCheck={false}
113:           onChange={(event) => setQuery(event.target.value)}
114:         />
115:         <button
116:           className={"glyph-toggle" + (caseSensitive ? " is-active" : "")}
117:           title="match case"
118:           onClick={() => setCaseSensitive((value) => !value)}
119:         >
120:           Aa
121:         </button>
122:         <button
123:           className={"glyph-toggle" + (regex ? " is-active" : "")}
124:           title="regular expression"
125:           onClick={() => setRegex((value) => !value)}
126:         >
127:           .*
128:         </button>
129:         <button className="link" onClick={close}>
130:           close
131:         </button>
132:       </div>
133: 
134:       {note() && <div className="folder-search-note">{note()}</div>}
135: 
136:       {answer?.files.map((file) => (
137:         <div key={file.path}>
138:           <div className="folder-search-file">
139:             <span className="folder-search-name">{file.name}</span>
140:             <span className="folder-search-where">{folderOf(file.rel)}</span>
141:           </div>
142:           {file.matches.map((match) => (
143:             <button
144:               key={`${match.line}`}
145:               className="folder-search-line"
146:               onClick={() => {
147:                 // The screen has the content area, so it has to step aside
148:                 // before the line it points at can be shown.
149:                 void openInEdit(file.path).then(() => {
150:                   useStore.getState().setFolderSearch(false);
151:                   // A frame later the editor is mounted and measured, so the
152:                   // jump scrolls instead of only moving the caret.
153:                   requestAnimationFrame(() => emitGotoLine(match.line));
154:                 });
155:               }}
156:             >
157:               <span className="folder-search-no">{match.line}</span>
158:               <Line match={match} />
159:             </button>
160:           ))}
161:         </div>
162:       ))}
163:     </div>
164:   );
165: }

34: }

36: function commandEntries(query: string, close: () => void): Entry[] {
37:   const needle = query.trim().toLowerCase();
38:   return availableCommands()
39:     .filter((command) => command.title.toLowerCase().includes(needle))
40:     .map((command: AppCommand) => ({
41:       key: `action:${command.id}`,
42:       label: plain(command.title),
43:       where: (command.chord ?? command.hint ?? "").toLowerCase(),
44:       run: () => {
45:         close();
46:         void command.run();
47:       },
48:     }));
49: }

51: export function QuickSearch() {
52:   const open = useStore((s) => s.quickSearch);
53:   const tree = useStore((s) => s.tree);
54:   const recent = useStore((s) => s.recent);
55:   const libraryPath = useStore((s) => s.libraryPath);
56: 
57:   const [query, setQuery] = useState("");
58:   const modal = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
59:   // cmdk calls `onSelect` without the event, so the modifier is read here.
60:   const withCtrl = useRef(false);
61: 
62:   useEffect(() => {
63:     setQuery(open?.seed ?? "");
64:   }, [open]);
65: 
66:   const close = () => useStore.getState().setQuickSearch(null);
67: 
68:   const paths = useMemo(() => files(tree), [tree]);
69: 
70:   const sections = useMemo(() => {
71:     if (!open) return [];
72:     if (query.startsWith(">")) {
73:       return [{ title: "actions", entries: commandEntries(query.slice(1), close) }];
74:     }
75:     if (query.trim() === "") {
76:       const entries: Entry[] = recent.slice(0, RECENT).map((path) => ({
77:         key: `recent:${path}`,
78:         label: plain(basename(path)),
79:         where: dirname(path),
80:         run: (inEdit) => {
81:           close();
82:           void (inEdit ? openInEdit(path) : openPaths([path]));
83:         },
84:       }));
85:       return [{ title: "recent", entries }];
86:     }
87: 
88:     const haystack = paths.map((node) => node.rel);
89:     const entries: Entry[] = rank(haystack, query).map((hit) => {
90:       const node = paths[hit.index];
91:       const rel = haystack[hit.index] ?? "";
92:       return {
93:         key: `file:${rel}`,
94:         label: pieces(rel, hit.ranges),
95:         where: folderOf(rel),
96:         run: (inEdit) => {
97:           close();
98:           if (!node) return;
99:           void (inEdit ? openInEdit(node.path) : openPaths([node.path]));
100:         },
101:       };
102:     });
103:     // Without a library there is nothing to search but the commands (�4).
104:     if (!libraryPath) {
105:       return [{ title: "actions", entries: commandEntries(query, close) }];
106:     }
107:     return [{ title: "files", entries }];
108:     // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
109:   }, [open, query, paths, recent, libraryPath]);
110: 
111:   // A click anywhere else is a way out, like `Esc`.
112:   useEffect(() => {
113:     if (!open) return;
114:     const onDown = (event: MouseEvent) => {
115:       if (!modal.current?.contains(event.target as Node)) close();
116:     };
117:     window.addEventListener("mousedown", onDown);
118:     return () => window.removeEventListener("mousedown", onDown);
119:   }, [open]);
120: 
121:   if (!open) return null;
122: 
123:   const empty = sections.every((section) => section.entries.length === 0);
124: 
125:   return (
126:     <Command
127:       className="qs"
128:       ref={modal}
129:       label="quick search"
130:       shouldFilter={false}
131:       loop
132:       onKeyDown={(event) => {
133:         if (event.key === "Escape") {
134:           event.preventDefault();
135:           event.stopPropagation();
136:           close();
137:           return;
138:         }
139:         if (event.key === "Enter") withCtrl.current = event.ctrlKey;
140:       }}
141:     >
142:       <div className="qs-field">
143:         <span className="qs-glyph">�?</span>
144:         <Command.Input
145:           className="qs-input"
146:           value={query}
147:           onValueChange={setQuery}
148:           placeholder="search files, or > for commands"
149:           autoFocus
150:         />
151:         <span className="qs-esc">esc</span>
152:       </div>
153: 
154:       <Command.List className="qs-list">
155:         {empty && <Command.Empty className="qs-empty">nothing found</Command.Empty>}
156:         {sections.map((section) =>
157:           section.entries.length === 0 ? null : (
158:             <Command.Group
159:               key={section.title}
160:               heading={<span className="qs-section">{section.title}</span>}
161:             >
162:               {section.entries.map((entry) => (
163:                 <Command.Item
164:                   key={entry.key}
165:                   value={entry.key}
166:                   className="qs-item"
167:                   onSelect={() => {
168:                     const inEdit = withCtrl.current;
169:                     withCtrl.current = false;

172:                 >

176:                         {piece.text}
177:                       </span>
178:                     ))}
179:                   </span>
180:                   {entry.where && <span className="qs-where">{entry.where}</span>}
181:                 </Command.Item>
182:               ))}
183:             </Command.Group>
184:           ),

22: function NameField({
23:   initial,
24:   depth,
25:   onDone,
26:   onCancel,
27: }: {
28:   initial: string;
29:   depth: number;
30:   onDone: (name: string) => void;
31:   onCancel: () => void;
32: }) {
33:   const input = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
34:   const [value, setValue] = useState(initial);
35: 
36:   useEffect(() => {
37:     const field = input.current;
38:     if (!field) return;
39:     field.focus();
40:     // The extension is rarely what you want to retype.
41:     const dot = initial.lastIndexOf(".");
42:     field.setSelectionRange(0, dot > 0 ? dot : initial.length);
43:   }, [initial]);
44: 
45:   return (
46:     <div className="tree-row" style={indent(depth)}>
47:       <input
48:         ref={input}
49:         className="tree-input"
50:         value={value}
51:         spellCheck={false}
52:         onChange={(event) => setValue(event.target.value)}
53:         onBlur={onCancel}
54:         onKeyDown={(event) => {
55:           if (event.key === "Enter") {
56:             event.preventDefault();
57:             onDone(value);
58:           } else if (event.key === "Escape") {
59:             event.preventDefault();
60:             event.stopPropagation();
61:             onCancel();
62:           }
63:         }}
64:       />
65:     </div>
66:   );
